cl_report.d: The national centre for adverse event reporting, part of the WHO programme. Reports from patients are accepted in most member countries.

fe_register.d: The regional society, which runs training and publishes regional data where national registers do not exist. ASPIRE covers the Asia-Pacific and its data are drawn from members who choose to report, so coverage varies sharply by country. One point applies to every professional register in this category: it is not a licence. A clinic missing from it may simply not have joined, and a clinic in it has met a society's conditions rather than a state's. Where a country has no statutory regulator, this is the best record available and also not a register of who is permitted to practise.

cl_find.d: The drug administration authorises trials. The link goes to the WHO ICTRP search portal, which aggregates this registry rather than being it; the national registry's own site has not been verified here.

decides.d: Handles approvals. Pakistan grows engineered cotton at scale, much of it from seed that entered the country before any approval — adoption preceding registration, as in Paraguay.

complain.n: Provincial agriculture and food departments — seed
complain.d: Seed inspection and enforcement is provincial, and the provincial power over seed is real enough to have stopped movement between provinces. In late 2025 the Punjab Food Department blocked transport of certified wheat seed out of Rahim Yar Khan, a district supplying more than 60 per cent of the certified wheat seed used by other provinces; trucks stood at provincial borders for days, the Seed Association of Pakistan went to the Lahore High Court, and the department continued the blockade after the federal Ministry of National Food Security and Research had directed it to release the consignments. Federal inspection teams do work alongside provincial ones on fake seed, but the province holds the decision.

complain.n: Provincial food authorities — Punjab (PFA) and Sindh (SFA)
complain.d: Food safety is provincial in Pakistan and the two largest provinces run statutory authorities that take complaints from the public directly. The Punjab Food Authority was created by the Punjab Food Authority Act 2011 and sits under the provincial Food Department; the Sindh Food Authority was created by the Sindh Food Authority Act 2016, began operating in 2018 in Karachi and Larkana and has extended division by division since, reaching Sukkur and Benazirabad in 2023 — so coverage inside Sindh is recent and uneven rather than province-wide from the start. Punjab has since also stood up a separate Agriculture, Food and Drug Authority with its own complaint process. These bodies act on food as sold: labelling, hygiene and adulteration. None of them authorises a release. Food safety is provincial in Pakistan; Punjab and Sindh food authorities take labelling complaints.

certify.d: Small and export-oriented. Search it by country of operation rather than by country of origin: in most places the certificate a grower actually holds is issued by a multinational certifier working locally, not by a body founded there, and the national names in this category are only part of the picture.

legal.n: Roots for Equity, PKMT and the Pakistan Kissan Rabita Committee
legal.d: Works with smallholder growers on seed and cotton, in a country where much of the engineered crop arrived before approval. Roots for Equity works with PAKISTAN KISSAN MAZDOOR TEHREEK (PKMT), a movement of small and landless farmers, and its campaigns have been on corporate control of the dairy and livestock sector as well as on land. Beside it, the PAKISTAN KISSAN RABITA COMMITTEE (PKRC) is LA VÍA CAMPESINA'S ONLY MEMBER IN PAKISTAN, a network of around 27–30 small farmers' organisations formed in 2003 at a conference of over 5,000 farmers at Chishtian in Punjab. Its origin is worth knowing because it shows the method working: it grew out of the successful 2000–01 LAND RIGHTS CAMPAIGN ON THE 17,000-ACRE MILITARY FARMS IN OKARA DISTRICT, where farmers had cultivated for over a century — the lesson drawn being that a campaign in one or two districts could not hold without a national body. PKRC also works on displacement of small farmers by mega-projects. Note PKRC's membership is broad: it includes the Farmers Association of Pakistan, described elsewhere as a landlords' lobbying organisation, so the network is not uniformly a smallholder voice.

test.n: National Institute for Biotechnology and Genetic Engineering
test.d: Runs detection; much of the engineered cotton in Pakistan arrived before approval. Founded 1994 at Faisalabad, one of four bioscience centres operated by the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission, with divisions including agricultural biotechnology and technical services providing analytical capability. It is an affiliated centre of ICGEB. Worth noting who runs it: the country's main plant biotechnology institute sits under the atomic energy commission, an arrangement that also holds in several other states and is invisible from the institute's name.

cl_find.d: Pakistan's medicines regulator, an autonomous body formed under the DRAP Act 2012, maintains a registry of approved trials under Rule 20 of the Bio-Study Rules 2017. But it has adopted the US ClinicalTrials.gov register as its international registry: sponsors are required to enlist approved trials there, obtain an NCT identifier and report that number back to DRAP. So the searchable record of Pakistani trials is held in another country's system by design, not by omission. Participant identities are submitted directly to the regulator and withheld from the investigator, to stop duplicate enrolment.

decides.d: Assesses applications and issues a biosafety recommendation to the Minister of Environment and the other authorised ministers, who then take the decision on release and circulation — so the Commission does not itself authorise anything, and a recommendation is not the decision. Nineteen members drawn from government, universities and the public, appointed by presidential decision. Its plenary sittings and the products considered at them are posted to the Indonesia Biosafety Clearing-House.
Issues the release decision.

complain.n: Barantin — Badan Karantina Indonesia (quarantine and seed inspection)
complain.d: Inspects imports and seed. THE NAME AND THE PARENT BOTH CHANGED: Barantin became a CABINET-LEVEL agency on 20 July 2023, merging the agricultural quarantine agency from the agriculture ministry with the fish quarantine agency from marine affairs and fisheries, so anything citing karantina.pertanian.go.id or an agriculture-ministry quarantine body predates that. Seed is the reason to write here rather than to BPOM: quarantine covers what arrives as planting material, while BPOM covers food and labelling on the market. Testing is done by Barantin's own Balai Besar Uji Standar, the standards-testing laboratory for animal, fish and plant quarantine, which also runs proficiency testing for other laboratories — named separately in this country's testing entry. One caution about the IPPC record often cited for this contact: it is updated by the country itself and can lag, so take the named person, address and telephone and check the institutional name against the agency's own site.

complain.n: BPOM — Badan Pengawas Obat dan Makanan
complain.d: Handles food labelling and safety complaints. A national agency reporting DIRECTLY TO THE PRESIDENT rather than through a ministry, coordinating with the health minister — an unusual place in the machinery for a food regulator, and worth knowing because it means no ministry sits between a complaint and the decision. Its supervision covers sampling, testing and laboratory analysis of food and beverages for hazardous substances, and compliance with safety, quality and LABELLING requirements, at both pre-market and post-market stages. It works through a tiered network of technical units — Balai Besar POM, Balai POM and Loka POM — so there is an office below the national level. It also runs a Directorate of Food and Drug Intelligence and a Directorate of Cyber, the latter covering products sold online, which few bodies in this category name at all.

certify.d: Certification bodies accredited under the Indonesian national organic standard. Accredited under the national organic standard. Search it by country of operation rather than by country of origin: in most places the certificate a grower actually holds is issued by a multinational certifier working locally, not by a body founded there, and the national names in this category are only part of the picture.

legal.d: Works on seed law and trade agreement provisions affecting smallholder seed saving. Formed 7 August 2001 (formerly Institute for Global Justice) to work on trade liberalisation, and registered as an association by notarial act in 2002. Its priorities are the reason it belongs here: the WTO AGREEMENT ON AGRICULTURE and TRIPS — trade-related intellectual property — alongside GATS, market access, investment and competition policy. TRIPS is the instrument behind plant variety protection obligations, so this is the address for the TRADE AND PATENT side of a seed dispute rather than the field side. It works by research feeding advocacy and public education, and convenes civil-society coalitions. Current themes include trade and investment agreements, business and human rights, and CORPORATE MONOPOLY.

test.d: The quarantine agency runs import testing. Its Balai Besar Uji Standar is the standards-testing laboratory for animal, fish and plant quarantine, accredited through the national accreditation committee and running proficiency testing for other laboratories, including detection and identification work. A laboratory that sets the proficiency test for others is the reference point in that country.

decides.n: Department of Agriculture — Bureau of Plant Industry
decides.d: Authorises releases. In 2024 the Court of Appeals revoked the approvals for Golden Rice and Bt eggplant through a constitutional environmental remedy citizens can invoke directly — the only case anywhere of a court withdrawing a granted biosafety approval at the public's request.

complain.n: BPI — Bureau of Plant Industry, and its Plant Product Safety Services Division
complain.d: Inspect and enforce locally. Republic Act No. 10611, the Food Safety Act of 2013, makes BPI a FOOD SAFETY REGULATORY AGENCY, and its Plant Product Safety Services Division covers fresh and minimally processed plant foods from primary production through post-harvest. The division is the practical address: it licenses food business operators and cold storage warehouses, runs PhilGAP certification, accredits plant food testing laboratories, and provides ANALYSIS OF PESTICIDE RESIDUES, microbiological contaminants, chemical contaminants and pesticide formulation. Four regional pesticide analysis laboratories cover the country. BPI's wider mandate names the seed side too — plant genetic resources, variety registration, accreditation of private plant nurseries, seed quality assurance, plant quarantine, and REGULATING PRODUCTS OF PLANT BIOTECHNOLOGY. Note two domains: buplant.da.gov.ph and bpi.da.gov.ph.

complain.n: FDA Philippines
complain.d: Handles food labelling complaints.

certify.n: OCCP — Organic Certification Center of the Philippines
certify.d: The national organic certifier under the Organic Agriculture Act.

notice.n: Bureau of Plant Industry — public notices
notice.d: Applications carry a public notice and comment period, which is what the 2024 court case turned on.

legal.d: A network of farmers and scientists breeding rice collectively and keeping it out of the patent system, and one of the petitioners in the case that revoked the Golden Rice approval in 2024. It is the clearest example anywhere of farmers doing the breeding themselves rather than choosing between varieties others bred.

test.d: Runs seed and crop testing for enforcement.

decides.n: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment
decides.d: Authorises environmental release; the agriculture ministry handles cultivation. Vietnam approved engineered maize in 2014 and grows a modest area while importing several million tonnes of engineered maize and soy each year for feed. The Clearing-House entry in this box explains what a country profile holds and what a thin one means.

complain.n: Cục Trồng trọt và Bảo vệ thực vật — Crop Production and Plant Protection Department
complain.d: Founded 1961 and now merged with crop production — the department is Cục Trồng trọt và Bảo vệ thực vật, no longer the Plant Protection Department alone, and it sits under the Ministry of Agriculture and ENVIRONMENT rather than Agriculture and Rural Development, following the 2025 reorganisation. Older citations, including the IPPC contact record, use the previous names. Its remit is the widest of the Vietnamese bodies in this file: pest control, plant quarantine, PESTICIDE registration, FERTILISER management, and food safety for plant-origin products from primary production through harvest, preliminary processing, storage, transport and trade, plus import and export food safety checks. 149 Hồ Đắc Di, Đống Đa, Hanoi, with a representative office in Ho Chi Minh City.

complain.n: VFA — Vietnam Food Administration (Cục An toàn thực phẩm)
complain.d: Under the health ministry, with its own legal personality, responsible for state management of food safety for domestic and imported food nationwide. Its published work includes investigating suspected poisoning incidents and issuing warnings on specific products, so a complaint here reaches a body that acts on individual cases rather than only on standards. Testing sits in a separate institution: the National Institute for Food Control, established 2009, is the health sector's highest-level food testing unit — a sample and a complaint go to different addresses. Its current functions are fixed by Decision No. 3668/QĐ-BYT of 28 September 2023; note the official English name is Vietnam Food ADMINISTRATION, though Food Safety Authority is widely used. It is the standing agency of the Central Inter-ministerial Steering Committee on food safety. A practical route exists: a national FOOD SAFETY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM, built with Korea's MFDS and operational since March 2024, includes an online reporting system, a channel for provincial and municipal authorities to report FOOD POISONING INCIDENTS online, and a portal handling complaints and feedback, advertisement monitoring and food safety warnings, with laboratory information integrated. Two cautions. Responsibility is split three ways under Decree 15/2018/ND-CP — health takes six product categories, with industry and trade and agriculture and environment holding the rest — and the structure is IN FLUX: provincial Divisions of Food Safety began being disbanded in late 2025 into Food Safety Offices under local health departments, and a May 2026 draft scheme proposes making the VFA the single coordinating authority. Check which office is current locally before writing.

certify.d: Coordinates certification under the national organic standard. The link goes to the IFOAM certifiers directory, searchable by country, rather than to this certifier's own site, which has not been verified here. Search it by country of operation rather than by country of origin: in most places the certificate a grower actually holds is issued by a multinational certifier working locally, not by a body founded there, and the national names in this category are only part of the picture. test.n: NAFIQAD — National Agro-Forestry-Fisheries Quality Assurance Department
test.d: Runs food and feed testing, which is where the imported engineered maize and soy arrives. Under the agriculture and rural development ministry, it runs testing and certification for agricultural, forestry and fishery products, and its certification is what opens export markets that require an official assurance. Two other bodies hold the neighbouring ground and a reader should know which they want: the health ministry's Vietnam Food Safety Authority takes complaints about food on sale, and the National Institute for Food Control does the health sector's testing.

cl_find.d: Authorises trials. The link goes to the WHO ICTRP search portal, which aggregates this registry rather than being it; the national registry's own site has not been verified here.

decides.d: Handles applications. Thailand permits field trials but has not authorised commercial cultivation, while remaining a large exporter of rice and a major feed importer.

complain.n: Department of Agriculture (กรมวิชาการเกษตร) and its Plant Protection Research and Development Office
complain.d: Inspect seed and crops. The DOA is Thailand's national plant protection organisation and holds SEED QUALITY CONTROL and PLANT VARIETY PROTECTION as well as plant health, so variety and seed questions go to the same department. Three named offices to distinguish: the PLANT PROTECTION RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT OFFICE (PPRDO) covers surveillance, PEST OUTBREAKS AND INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT; the OFFICE OF AGRICULTURAL REGULATION runs plant quarantine operations; and a Plant Quarantine Research Group sits within PPRDO. The PLANT ACT B.E. 2518 is the instrument behind export control of wild plant populations — it has been used on wild orchid exports. Two current threads worth knowing: the DEPARTMENT PUBLISHES DRAFT ANNOUNCEMENTS FOR PUBLIC COMMENT on its site, which is a live consultation route; and it administers the RESTRICTION MEASURES ON THREE SUBSTANCES — PARAQUAT, GLYPHOSATE AND CHLORPYRIFOS. PPRDO also rears PREDATORY INSECTS and studies the impact of pesticides on them. 50 Phaholyothin Road, Chatuchak, Bangkok 10900.

complain.n: Thai FDA
complain.d: Handles food labelling complaints.

certify.d: The main Thai certifier, and IFOAM-accredited, so its certificate is recognised abroad.

legal.d: Tracks seed law, plant variety protection and trade agreements, and is the source most Thai reporting on this draws from.

test.d: Runs seed and crop detection; Thailand permits trials but no commercial cultivation.

fe_register.n: Protection for Children Born through ART Act, B.E. 2558 (2015) — and the PMRT Committee
fe_register.d: Thailand prohibited commercial surrogacy for foreigners in 2015 after the Baby Gammy case, having been a principal destination for it. Enacted 19 February 2015 and in force ninety days after gazette publication. Oversight sits with a statutory committee — the Committee for Protection of a Child Born by Medically Assisted Reproductive Technology — chaired by the Permanent Secretary of Public Health with the President of the Medical Council as vice-chair, and including the social development ministry, the national children's protection committee and the royal colleges of paediatricians, psychiatrists and obstetricians. Conditions: only married couples, at least three years married, with a Thai partner; the surrogate must be a relative of an intended parent; no direct payment to her; at least one intended parent must be genetically related. Penalties reach ten years' imprisonment. The linked English text is an unofficial translation by the Council of State's Law for ASEAN project and says so — the Thai original governs.

decides.d: Handles agricultural approvals; the food ministry handles food use. Korea is one of the largest importers of engineered maize and soy in the world and grows none commercially.

complain.n: MFDS — Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (food labelling complaints)
complain.d: Korea labels engineered food and this is where a complaint about one goes. In a country growing none commercially, labelling is where nearly every dispute arises. Formed 12 March 2013 from the Korea Food and Drug Administration, so citations to the KFDA predate it; headquartered at Cheongju, and it publishes an English site including the Food Sanitation Act, its enforcement decree and the Labelling Standards for Foods. Two mechanisms matter for imported material. Anyone importing food, or operating a foreign food facility supplying Korea, must REGISTER, and a facility with a history of non-compliant exports can be inspected on site — a refusal or non-response within the stated window is itself treated as grounds. And where products bought directly online are found to contain harmful substances, MFDS asks Customs to withhold them and PUBLISHES the list on FoodSafetyKorea. A published list of withheld products is rarer than a complaint line.

certify.d: Under the national environment-friendly agriculture scheme. Search it by country of operation rather than by country of origin: in most places the certificate a grower actually holds is issued by a multinational certifier working locally, not by a body founded there, and the national names in this category are only part of the picture.

legal.d: Campaigns on imported feed and labelling, which is the live question in a country that grows none commercially.

test.d: The food and drug ministry runs the testing behind Korea's labelling enforcement.

notice.d: Korea's national node, which publishes approvals and risk assessments in Korean and English.

cl_find.d: The Korean national registry.

an_inspect.n: Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency — animal experiment ethics
an_inspect.d: Registers institutions and publishes national animal-use statistics. Formed 15 June 2011 by merger, under the agriculture, food and rural affairs ministry, and it publishes the national animal-use statistics. Two things a reader should expect. The published data are in Korean only — researchers translating them note that, and the figures they carry are substantial: institutions operating animal facilities rising year on year, and animals used for education and research going from about 2.5 million in 2015 to about 4.9 million in 2021, roughly 90% of the rodents being mice. And the series has gaps: 2017 is absent from the published years. A national total that skips a year is still the best figure available, and the gap should travel with it.

lab_oversight.d: The disease control agency licenses and inspects high-containment facilities. Two separate regimes run in parallel and a reader needs the right one. Under the LMO Act, anyone setting up or operating a facility that develops or experiments with living modified organisms must be licensed or must notify, depending on the containment grade; for LMOs hazardous to humans at biosafety levels 3 and 4 the licence comes from the KDCA commissioner. Under the infectious disease law, facilities handling listed high-risk pathogens at levels 3 and 4 need the commissioner's licence too, and any change to a licensed matter needs re-licensing. Levels 1 and 2 are notification rather than licence. LINK CHECKED AND FOUND DEAD: the page or host no longer answers. The body may well still exist — government sites move and rename constantly — so confirm through the worldwide routes in this box, or the Biosafety Clearing-House or IPPC contact page for this country, rather than treating the absence as evidence the body has gone.

cl_report.n: Korea Institute of Drug Safety and Risk Management
cl_report.d: The national centre for adverse event reporting, part of the WHO programme. Reports from patients are accepted in most member countries.

decides.d: Authorises under the Biosafety Law. Turkey prohibits cultivation of engineered crops entirely while approving specific events for animal feed — one of the clearest splits between what may be grown and what may be imported. The Clearing-House entry in this box explains what a country profile holds and what a thin one means.

complain.n: Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (Türkiye) — Gıda ve Kontrol Genel Müdürlüğü
complain.d: Inspects and enforces. The General Directorate of Food and Control is the unit inside the ministry that does this work, and its own service list names the parts: plant health services, veterinary services, food and feed services, the ALO 174 line, the food safety information system, the plant protection products database, and a published list of analysis services. The ministry itself was formed in 2018 by merging the Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Livestock with the Ministry of Forestry and Water Management, so older citations name one of those.

complain.n: ALO 174 Gıda Hattı — the food complaint line
complain.d: Turkey runs a dedicated food complaint line; cultivation is prohibited, so what arrives is the question. Running since 14 February 2009 and open 24 hours. Five ways in: the 174 line from anywhere in Turkey, a WhatsApp number, e-mail, live chat on the site, and a mobile app — and a complaint can be tracked afterwards by reference number or national ID. Complaints are routed by content either to the ministry or to contact points designated in all 81 provinces, and the outcome is recorded in the same system. The published figures are unusually complete: from 2009 to 12 January 2026 the line took 3,392,521 calls, of which 1,273,008 were registered as food complaints and 1,267,167 resolved. Note it is CHARGED, at an agreed lowest tariff, deliberately — to deter false and off-topic calls; the e-mail, chat and app routes are free.

certify.d: Accredited under the national organic regulation; Turkey prohibits cultivation entirely, so certification concerns imports and processing. Search it by country of operation rather than by country of origin: in most places the certificate a grower actually holds is issued by a multinational certifier working locally, not by a body founded there, and the national names in this category are only part of the picture.

test.d: Ministry laboratories run the detection behind Turkey's feed approvals and cultivation ban.

legal.d: Works on the biosafety law and organic agriculture; Turkey bans cultivation while approving feed.

Several states in the region restrict treatment to married couples and prohibit donation entirely, so what is lawful differs sharply across a short distance. One point applies to every professional register in this category: it is not a licence. A clinic missing from it may simply not have joined, and a clinic in it has met a society's conditions rather than a state's. Where a country has no statutory regulator, this is the best record available and also not a register of who is permitted to practise.

cl_find.d: The clinical trials portal of the Turkish medicines and medical devices agency, holding the trials that fall within its remit. Two limits are stated on the portal itself and matter before relying on it: the published data are for information only, and where they disagree with the agency's own records the agency's records prevail; and the current version carries applications made from 2016 onward, excluding studies that ended before 1 January 2020 and bioavailability and bioequivalence studies altogether. Trials are approved by ethics committees the agency itself authorises, with ministry permission.

decides.d: Authorises. Chile permits engineered seed to be grown only for export multiplication, not for domestic planting — so a field of it here is producing seed for somebody else's country, which is a distinction most registers do not make.

complain.n: SAG regional offices
complain.d: Inspect and enforce locally.

complain.n: SEREMI de Salud
complain.d: Regional health authorities handle food labelling complaints. The regional health secretariat in each region enforces the food sanitary regulation, Decree 977 of 1996, whose 543 articles cover labelling rules, additives, microbiological specifications and penalties. The link goes to the health ministry's own complaints page rather than one region's office, since which secretariat applies depends on where you are. Analysis is separate again: the Instituto de Salud Pública acts as the national reference laboratory for food and runs chemical, microbiological and toxicological tests at the request of the ministry, the regional secretariats, the food safety agency or the consumer service.

certify.d: Accredited under the national organic law, largely for export fruit and wine. Search it by country of operation rather than by country of origin: in most places the certificate a grower actually holds is issued by a multinational certifier working locally, not by a body founded there, and the national names in this category are only part of the picture.

legal.n: Yo No Quiero Transgénicos — and RAP-Chile
legal.d: Campaigns on the seed export multiplication regime, which is unusual in permitting growing without permitting planting. The campaign that carries this work in Chile is YO NO QUIERO TRANSGÉNICOS, running with RAP-Chile (the pesticide action network affiliate). It maintains an active archive indexed by subject — labelling, glyphosate, seed savers, SAG decisions, moratorium, constitutional court, ANPROS, monopoly, contamination — which makes it a usable research route rather than only a campaign page. Two threads it has followed that this map documents: the LEY DE OBTENTORES VEGETALES (the 'Ley Monsanto'), opposed on the ground that it paves the way for transgenic crops and threatens peasant and indigenous seed — Chile having moved from UPOV 78 toward UPOV 91 under free-trade commitments — and the SAG's handling of new gene-editing rules, which it has reported as being settled without public participation.

notice.d: SAG resolutions authorising seed multiplication are published here — the regime that permits growing for export without permitting domestic planting.

test.d: Runs seed testing for the export multiplication regime, which is where most Chilean engineered seed is.

fe_register.d: The Latin American assisted reproduction network: it accredits clinics across the region, runs the continental registry of treatment cycles and outcomes, and publishes an annual report. Across most of Latin America there is no statutory fertility regulator at all, so an accreditation held or withdrawn here is the only external check on a clinic — and the accredited list is public. One point applies to every professional register in this category: it is not a licence. Where a country has no statutory regulator, this is the best record available and also not a register of who is permitted to practise.

It states a limit of its own worth quoting: it cannot vouch for the safety of unregistered food, food that entered without control, or food acquired illegally — and Paraguayan reporting describes importers using court injunctions against the sanitary rules to bring products in outside the registration system. A complaint about a registered product and one about a product that bypassed registration are not the same problem.

complain.n: MGAP — Dirección General de Servicios Agrícolas (DGSA)
complain.d: Inspects and enforces. The Dirección General de Servicios Agrícolas is the unit that handles agrochemical complaints, at Avda. Millán 4703, Montevideo, and it is also Uruguay's IPPC contact. The published record shows the route works and how heavily it is used: MGAP recorded 758 denuncias between 2011 and 2017 resulting in 131 economic sanctions, annual figures rising from 35 in 2011 to 166 in 2017, with 21 in the first eight months of 2021. It applies fines and uses SATELLITE MONITORING to detect improper applications — a detection method few bodies in this category have. A 2013 civil ruling ordered compensation from a spraying firm after a rural school was exposed to drift from adjacent soy fields. Animal products are a separate directorate, the Dirección General de Servicios Ganaderos.

complain.n: Ministerio de Salud Pública — bromatología
complain.d: Municipal bromatology services handle food labelling; Uruguay runs a coexistence and traceability system. The ministry's food hygiene department sets and enforces the rules, but bromatología in Uruguay is substantially municipal: the Intendencia de Montevideo runs its own food and health service for the capital, and other departments do likewise, so a complaint about a product on a shelf often goes to the local authority rather than to the ministry. Agricultural production sits with the livestock, agriculture and fisheries ministry instead, and the Laboratorio Tecnológico del Uruguay does much of the analysis. THE COMPLAINT USUALLY BELONGS TO THE DEPARTMENT, NOT THE MINISTRY. The health ministry holds the normative competence under its Ley Orgánica Nº 9202 of 1934, and the REGLAMENTO BROMATOLÓGICO NACIONAL (Decreto 315/994) sets composition, LABELLING — composition, expiry, batch and origin — hygiene, and the registration every food business must hold; it is aligned to Codex. But Uruguay's NINETEEN DEPARTMENTAL GOVERNMENTS carry the food control inside their own territory, each with a Bromatología office that registers products, inspects premises and TAKES DENUNCIAS. Montevideo's Departamento de Regulación Alimentaria is the largest. What that produces is measurable: in one half-year it carried out 3,914 inspections of food premises, of which 15% (586) FOLLOWED A COMPLAINT, sanctioning 148 businesses with 541 fines and 23 CLOSURES. Non-compliance can bring sanctions, seizure of product and closure of the premises. The agriculture ministry (MGAP) holds the production side, including PESTICIDE REGISTRATION AND CORRECT USE IN THE FIELD — named separately in this box.

complain.n: SENASAG — Servicio Nacional de Sanidad Agropecuaria e Inocuidad Alimentaria
complain.d: Handles food labelling; Bolivia permits one soy event inside a constitution that restricts them. Food and agricultural health service; inspects and enforces. Created by Ley N° 2061 of 16 March 2000 and confirmed by LEY N° 830 of 6 September 2016, which declares agricultural health and food safety a national priority and names SENASAG THE NATIONAL COMPETENT AUTHORITY for it — a deconcentrated public institution under the Ministry of Desarrollo Rural y Tierras. Article 11 gives it a food safety component covering production and processing, good practices in primary production and transformation, registration and surveillance; and it can declare a PUBLIC EMERGENCY in agricultural health or food safety. It attends denuncias of notifiable diseases, takes official microbiological and physico-chemical samples as part of granting a registro sanitario, and works through departmental offices — Potosí and the others — with technical units for animal health, plant health and food safety. One body for the field and the shelf, which is rare in this file.

legal.n: RAAA — Red de Acción en Agricultura Alternativa (Peru)
legal.d: Worked on the moratorium that now runs to 2035, the longest in force anywhere. A DECENTRALISED NATIONAL NETWORK of more than 60 members, headquartered in Lima but working across Peru, and part of the Consorcio Agroecológico Peruano. What it offers is stated as a service rather than a slogan: advice on designing CAMPAIGNS AND ADVOCACY ACTIONS in favour of agrobiodiversity, THE GMO MORATORIUM LAW, and on the health and environmental impacts of agrochemicals — so for a reader working on Peru's moratorium this is the body that has done it. It also runs research, training and FISCALIZACIÓN of pesticide use, and has worked to displace extremely and highly hazardous pesticides in favour of biopesticides and agroecological practice, with the Chillón valley as a documented case. Staff are named with their qualifications, which is unusual and makes the technical claim checkable.

decides.d: Authorises field trials. Israel permits research and trials but no commercial cultivation, while hosting a substantial plant biotechnology sector — and it approved cultivated meat earliest of anywhere.

complain.n: PPIS — Plant Protection and Inspection Services
complain.d: Handles phytosanitary matters BOTH WITHIN Israel and in foreign trade, which is the distinction that matters after several bodies in this category that work only at the border. It operates offices inside the country as well as in Israeli embassies, and is the national representative to the IPPC and to EPPO. Note the parent: the ministry is now the Ministry of Agriculture and FOOD SECURITY — it was Agriculture and Rural Development from 1992, and the IPPC contact record still uses the older name. Headquarters at Rishon LeZion, with the IPPC postal contact at Bet Dagan.

complain.n: Ministry of Health — National Food Service (Israel)
complain.d: Handles food labelling complaints. The national food service within the health ministry is the competent authority for food, and Israeli food and feed legislation has been progressively aligned with EU rules — so the substantive standard a complaint is measured against is often an adopted EU one rather than a purely domestic rule. Agricultural production and field trials sit with the agriculture ministry instead. The governing instrument is the PROTECTION OF PUBLIC HEALTH (FOOD) LAW 5776-2015, in force September 2016, which regulates production, import and sale of food and — the part that matters here — EXPRESSLY VESTS THE MINISTRY WITH AUTHORITY OVER GENETICALLY MODIFIED FOOD: import, sale and production. The NFS develops the standards and handles all inspection and enforcement for food on the market, including novel foods. The division with agriculture is stated in the same source: MOAG regulates SEEDS, veterinary biologics, fertilisers and livestock feed, and runs the safety assessment for plants with novel traits, while health runs it for novel foods. Two later changes to expect: the 2022 amendments opened a EUROPEAN TRACK from 1 January 2023, admitting food on a declaration of lawful marketing in Europe and transferring responsibility for safety to the importer; and the obligation of direct importer-manufacturer contact was cancelled. Under the Law the Director of Food Services publishes orders in the Official Gazette and on the website.

an_inspect.n: Council for Animal Experimentation
an_inspect.d: Licenses institutions and publishes annual figures on animal use. It exists because the Knesset amended the Cruelty to Animals Act in 1994 to regulate experimental animals. The amendment set purposes: experiments may only be carried out to promote health and medical science, reduce suffering, advance scientific research, or for testing and production. A stated purpose test is a different instrument from a licence condition — it limits what an experiment may be FOR, not only how it must be done — and few of the countries in this category have one written into primary law.

complain.n: Emirate-level food control — ADAFSA, Dubai Municipality and the other municipalities (UAE)
complain.d: Food inspection is municipal in the UAE; a labelling complaint goes to the emirate rather than the federal ministry. WHICH BODY DEPENDS ON THE EMIRATE, and there is no single national food address. In ABU DHABI it is ADAFSA, established 2019 from the former Abu Dhabi Food Control Authority, responsible for agriculture, food safety AND BIOSECURITY, including ANIMAL AND PLANT HEALTH — so plant questions and food questions go to the same authority there. In DUBAI and SHARJAH food safety sits with the respective MUNICIPALITIES, which oversee requirements and check that products carry CORRECT LABELS AND EXPIRY DATES. Imported food is inspected AT EMIRATE LEVEL at the point of entry: Dubai Municipality runs the Food Import and Re-export System (FIRS) with RISK-BASED assessment leading to document checks, physical inspection or laboratory testing; ADAFSA operates its own risk classification. Above them a NATIONAL FOOD SAFETY COMMITTEE sits under the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, which also recognises the bodies issuing organic certificates. ADAFSA has used its powers on plants directly — it has BANNED THE CULTIVATION, PROPAGATION AND CIRCULATION of oleander within the emirate.

fe_register.n: Federal Law 7/2019 as amended by Federal Decree-Law 17/2023 — medically assisted reproduction
fe_register.d: THIS ROW WAS OUT OF DATE. The restriction to married couples and the prohibition on surrogacy were amended by Federal Decree-Law 17 of 2023, in force 16 September 2023, which replaced eleven articles of the 2019 law. Article 8 now permits non-Muslim unmarried couples to undergo IVF, subject to proof that natural conception is impossible, prior written consent, and a certified declaration of the child's lineage from the competent authority of the country whose nationality the child will take. The explicit prohibition on surrogacy was removed without any federal framework replacing it, and each emirate may now legislate locally: Abu Dhabi's Department of Health issued a Standard for Gestational Surrogacy in February 2025, applying to its licensed hospitals and ART clinics, with commercial surrogacy still prohibited. The law reaches centres in FREE ZONES as well. Operating a suspended centre carries a fine of AED 200,000 to 500,000 and possible closure.

complain.n: Department of Agriculture (Jabatan Pertanian), Malaysia
complain.d: Inspects and enforces. Under the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, and it runs a department in each state, which is where an inspection actually starts. The ministry's other agencies split the rest: veterinary services for animals, fisheries, the quarantine and inspection department (MAQIS) for anything crossing the border, and MARDI for research. Malaysia also has an agro-biotechnology institute inside the same ministry, so the body developing engineered organisms and the body inspecting for them report to one minister.

complain.n: FSQD — Food Safety and Quality Division, Ministry of Health (Malaysia)
complain.d: Handles labelling complaints; Malaysia requires GM labelling. It implements and enforces the FOOD ACT 1983, whose Food Regulations 1985 set the labelling requirements this map cares about, and the Food Hygiene Regulations 2009 for premises. The programme runs at state, district, national and POINT-OF-ENTRY levels, with risk-based control over food entering the country — so an imported-grain question and a shelf question go to the same programme, at different tiers. Its stated purpose names fraud alongside health hazards. Analysis is a separate body: the Department of Chemistry Malaysia's Food Quality Division does the analytical work supporting enforcement of the 1985 Regulations, with SAMM-accredited methods. Food control here dates back to the Sale of Food and Drugs Ordinance 1952 and a Food Quality Control Unit formed in 1974.

complain.n: Ministry of Agriculture (Taiwan) — inspection
complain.d: Inspects seed and crops. The Council of Agriculture became the Ministry of Agriculture on 1 August 2023 — a reader following an older citation will not find the council. Agencies were renamed with it: the animal and plant health inspection body is now APHIA, and the Animal Health Research Institute became the National Veterinary Research Institute. Food safety is a separate authority again: the Taiwan FDA under the health and welfare ministry administers the food safety and sanitation act, while this ministry covers production and organic imports.

complain.n: TFDA — Food and Drug Administration (Taiwan), and the 1919 hotline
complain.d: Handles labelling complaints, and Taiwan additionally prohibits engineered ingredients in school meals. Formed 1 January 2010 by consolidating four bureaux — Food Safety, Pharmaceutical Affairs, Food and Drug Analysis, and Controlled Drugs — under the TFDA Organization Act, so citations to any of those predate it. The practical route is the 1919 NATIONAL FOOD SAFETY HOTLINE, reachable from fixed or mobile phones for a report, complaint or enquiry, and what happens next is published: reports are recorded as audio, registered as confidential and handled by a designated person, so the reporter's position is protected; cases involving criminal offences go to the Taiwan High Prosecutors Office and then to the district office, and non-criminal cases to the local Public Health Bureau. The hotline links to the central reporting line to trigger the inspection mechanism directly. Very few complaint routes in this file state both the confidentiality and the onward path.

decides.n: National Council for Science and Technology
decides.d: Approves confined field trials. Uganda has run trials for years — banana, cassava, maize — without a biosafety law in force, because successive bills were passed by parliament and not signed. Research proceeds; commercialisation cannot.

complain.n: MAAIF — Ministry of Agriculture
complain.d: Inspects seed and crops. The ministry site names its agencies, which matters here because the work is split: the Directorate of Agricultural Extension Services handles adoption and advice, the national research organisation coordinates research, and a separate animal genetic resources centre and databank leads on animal breeding. A question about an engineered animal and a question about an engineered crop go to different parts of the same ministry. The department to name is CROP INSPECTION AND CERTIFICATION (DCIC), which enforces the legislation on plants and plant products, SEEDS, PLANTING MATERIALS and agrochemicals, maintains plant quarantine facilities and SEED AND AGRO-CHEMICAL ANALYTICAL LABORATORIES, and takes produce samples for pesticide residue analysis — so the complaint and the test are in the same department. Under the AGRICULTURAL CHEMICALS (CONTROL) ACT 2006 no chemical may be imported or sold unless registered, packed and labelled to the regulations, and no person may sell without registered premises; MAAIF publishes the register of approved chemicals, dealers, premises and fumigators. It is also the lead agency within MAAIF advising on GMO regulatory decisions through UNCST, and under the Seeds and Plants Act recommends the procedures for varieties developed using new techniques. Expect a gap between rule and practice: an assessment found about 46% of agro-input dealers unregistered and 40% never trained in handling, and only about 35% of formal-sector seed certified.

complain.n: UNBS — Uganda National Bureau of Standards
complain.d: Handles food labelling standards; Uganda has no biosafety law in force, so this is often the only body that can act. Operational since 1 July 1989 under the UNBS Act Cap 327, a parastatal under the trade ministry, governed by the National Standards Council. Unlike Rwanda's board it KEPT its enforcement functions: its mandate is to formulate, promote AND ENFORCE standards in protection of public health, safety and the environment against dangerous and sub-standard products, and its services include import inspection, testing, certification and market surveillance. Two practical points: it is Uganda's FAO contact point and a WTO and ISO member, so it is also the enquiry route for a standards question; and forging or illegally using the UNBS Quality Mark carries a penalty of 10 to 50 million shillings. Toll free 0800133133. Standards are prepared through technical committees, one of which covers food, agriculture and forestry.

certify.d: The Ugandan organic movement, which certifies for export and runs participatory guarantee schemes domestically.

legal.d: Represents growers in the debate over the biosafety bill that has repeatedly passed parliament and not been signed. A national farmers' federation with a TOLL-FREE CALL CENTRE, which is a genuinely unusual thing for a membership body in this file to run and makes it reachable by a farmer with a phone and no internet. complain.n: TPHPA — Tanzania Plant Health and Pesticides Authority
complain.d: Inspects and enforces. One caution about this source: the IPPC contact record is updated by the country itself and can lag — records checked here carried ministry names that had since changed. The named person, address and telephone are the useful part; treat the institutional name as a starting point and check it against the ministry's own site. Established by the PLANT HEALTH ACT No. 4 of 2020, which repealed the Plant Protection Act 1998, merging the ministry's Plant Health Services with the Tropical Pesticides Research Institute into a single authority and making it Tanzania's national plant protection organisation. Powers a reader can use: it registers pesticides and gazettes the list, and where a REGISTERED pesticide has been shown to damage human health, animal health or the environment the Registrar may, on the Authority's recommendation, TEMPORARILY PROHIBIT its import, sale, distribution and use. It can re-evaluate a registration on reasonable grounds, and the Act covers substandard, counterfeit and adulterated pesticides, compensation for damage or loss suffered, and post-entry quarantine. Note a conflict-of-interest rule: board members, staff and agents may not trade in pesticides or regulated articles during their term or for one year after. Headquarters Ngaramtoni, Arusha; the old tpri.go.tz still resolves. LINK CHECKED AND FOUND DEAD: the page or host no longer answers. complain.n: Tanzania Bureau of Standards
complain.d: Handles food labelling standards and complaints. Established 1975 under the industry and trade ministry, with regional offices in Dodoma, Mwanza, Arusha, Mbeya and Mtwara as well as Dar es Salaam. Two things make it the practical route here. It is Tanzania's National Enquiry Point for the WTO technical barriers and sanitary and phytosanitary agreements, so it holds the technical regulations and proposed standards a reader would otherwise have to find country by country. And it runs product and premise registration and food risk assessment, which means it is the body a sample and a complaint both reach. IT DOES ENFORCE, and it gained the power recently. From 1 July 2019 the Finance Act amended the Standards Act No. 2 of 2009 and moved food and cosmetics regulation from the Tanzania Food and Drugs Authority to TBS — TFDA keeping medicines and devices and renaming itself the Tanzania Medicines and Medical Devices Authority. So anything citing TFDA for a food question predates July 2019. Under the amended Act NO PERSON MAY MANUFACTURE, IMPORT, DISTRIBUTE, SELL OR EXPOSE FOR SALE pre-packaged food unless the product is registered by the Bureau, and TBS registers production premises as well. Imports run through Pre-shipment Verification of Conformity under section 4(1)(s): consignments without a certificate of conformity are rejected or fined at the port. One caveat from a 2025 sector review: the amendment did not tidy the other food safety laws, so overlaps with TMDA persisted until a memorandum of understanding separated them. complain.n: Zambia Environmental Management Agency
complain.d: Handles environmental complaints. An independent environmental regulator established by the Environmental Management Act No. 12 of 2011, successor to the Environmental Council of Zambia, which administers the environmental impact assessment process and licenses pesticides and toxic substances. It publishes the environmental impact statements it receives in an online repository, including for commercial agriculture projects — so a reader can read what an applicant said before a decision was taken, which is rarer than it sounds.

complain.n: Zambia Bureau of Standards
complain.d: Handles food labelling standards and complaints. The national standards body, a statutory body under the trade ministry established in 1982 and mandated by the Standards Act No. 4 of 2017 for standardisation and conformity assessment. It runs testing and certification, and laboratory analysis for environmental monitoring — which is the practical answer in a country whose testing row otherwise points at regional laboratories abroad. On the enforcement question: ZABS describes its own services as standards development, conformity assessment, testing, certification, INSPECTION, metrology and training under the Standards Act No. 4 of 2017. Inspection is stated; a general power to act on a consumer complaint is not. For an environmental or release question the Zambia Environmental Management Agency, named in this country's other row, holds the statutory powers and publishes the environmental impact statements.

legal.n: ZAAB — Zambia Alliance for Agroecology and Biodiversity
legal.d: Works on seed law and farmer seed systems in the country that refused engineered food aid in 2002. ITS ORIGIN IS THE POINT: ZAAB was initiated in 2010 when civil society and farmer associations came together TO DEFEND ZAMBIA'S 'NO GMO' PRESIDENTIAL DECLARATION OF 2002 — the declaration behind Zambia's refusal of genetically modified maize food aid that year. It formalised under its present name in 2017. So this is an alliance built specifically around the position this map documents, still operating. A network of citizens, civil society, FAITH and farmer-based organisations, it publishes a members directory with profiles, which makes it a way to find the individual organisations — among them SCOPE Zambia, part of the regional ReSCOPE programme promoting FARMER SEED SYSTEMS across Kenya, Malawi, Uganda, Zambia and Zimbabwe, which has produced learning materials on SEED SAVING AND MULTIPLICATION. It publishes material on farmers' rights and on what allowing GMOs into the Zambian market would mean for small-scale farmers.

complain.n: Standards Association of Zimbabwe
complain.d: Handles labelling standards; imported grain must be milled before distribution. Formed 1957 and incorporated 1960, it is Zimbabwe's national standards body and — unusually for that role — a non-governmental, non-profit association rather than a state agency, staffed for standards work by technical committee members who serve without pay. It provides the WTO technical barriers enquiry point on the government's behalf, and runs testing of manufactured goods and raw materials. Food sample analysis sits elsewhere: the Government Analyst Laboratory under the health ministry tests food and water, and the Central Veterinary Laboratory handles animal-derived products.

legal.n: ZIMSOFF — Zimbabwe Smallholder Organic Farmers Forum
legal.d: Works on seed sovereignty in a country that mills imported grain rather than refusing it. Emerged in 2002 from a smallholder farmers' convergence held alongside the World Summit on Sustainable Development in Johannesburg. Its mission names the exact thing this map documents: influencing policy and public awareness toward agroecology and smallholder farmers' rights, and STRUGGLES FOR FARMER MANAGED SEED SYSTEMS. Membership has grown past 19,000, organised into four democratically structured regional clusters across EIGHT RURAL PROVINCES — so it reaches beyond the capital. It is a member of the East and Southern Africa Small-scale Farmers' Forum and of LA VÍA CAMPESINA, and HOSTED LA VÍA CAMPESINA'S INTERNATIONAL OPERATIVE SECRETARIAT FROM 2014; its president, Elizabeth Mpofu, served as La Vía Campesina's General Coordinator and farms at the SHASHE AGROECOLOGY SCHOOL in Masvingo district. That makes Zimbabwe a route into the global peasant movement, not only a national contact.

decides.d: The national competent authority for biosafety, a public scientific establishment under the ministry for scientific research. No GMO may be used in Burkina Faso without its prior authorisation, and it also carries out the inspections and audits that check whether an authorisation's conditions are being kept to. A decision runs through four bodies: the Comité Scientifique National de Biosécurité assesses the risk case by case and recommends, the Observatoire National de Biosécurité files its concerns, the ANB decides, and the public must be consulted before a release into the environment is authorised — so there is a stated point of entry rather than only an outcome. Burkina Faso grew Bt cotton at scale and withdrew it in 2016 because the fibre was shorter and worth less, the only case of a country abandoning a commercial engineered crop for quality reasons rather than safety or politics. Target Malaria's gene-drive mosquito work continues here, and the ANB has publicly backed the authorisations behind it. Its national biosafety laboratory is built as the UEMOA regional reference laboratory for GMO analysis, serving all eight member states. LINK REMOVED after a link check: the site no longer resolves. The body may still exist — confirm through the worldwide routes in this box, and through the Biosafety Clearing-House or IPPC contact page for this country, before assuming it has gone.

complain.n: Ministère de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources Animales et Halieutiques (MAERAH)
complain.d: Inspects and enforces. Phytosanitary protection of plants is among its listed services, and it publishes its own organigram naming the directorates and attached establishments — the reliable route here, because the ministry has been renamed repeatedly: Agriculture et Coopération, Agriculture et Ressources halieutiques, Agriculture et Aménagements hydro-agricoles, MARAH and now MAERAH have all been the same portfolio. Search the current site rather than an older acronym. Note also SOBIMAP, the state company for agro-pastoral inputs, sits under this ministry: the state supplies inputs and inspects them. The unit to name is the DIRECTION DE LA PROTECTION DES VÉGÉTAUX ET DU CONDITIONNEMENT (DPVC), which enforces the rules on import and sale of pesticides and runs UNANNOUNCED INSPECTIONS of shops with the police — a 2024 operation across Banfora and Bobo-Dioulasso seized unregistered and expired products, with officials attributing a mass entry of fraudulent product to porous borders under the security crisis. Two things beside it. What may lawfully be sold is set REGIONALLY by the Comité Sahélien des Pesticides, whose authorised list applies in Burkina Faso; a national Commission Nationale de Contrôle des Pesticides sits alongside. And for engineered organisms the address is the AGENCE NATIONALE DE BIOSÉCURITÉ (anb.bf), which has a director general and four technical directorates, and behind it the LABORATOIRE NATIONAL DE BIOSÉCURITÉ — built with a sub-regional remit as the reference laboratory for GMO detection and identification across the eight UEMOA states, and the intended hub of a regional laboratory network. That makes Burkina Faso a testing destination for its neighbours, not just for itself.

certify.d: Created 2011. Its BioSPG label, established 2013, is one of the first national organic labels in West Africa and works by participatory guarantee rather than third-party audit: producers, processors, transporters, distributors, consumers and support organisations all sit inside the verification, which is what makes it cheap enough to use. The standard was written with technical support from Helvetas and IFOAM, and the agriculture and trade ministries were involved. Between 2015 and 2024 it certified 1,622 producers; a 2024 bulletin reported 62 certified sites across 303 hectares. Set against the multinational certifiers elsewhere in this category, it is the alternative: certification a smallholder can afford, built by the people being certified.

legal.n: COPAGEN Burkina and the Collectif citoyen pour l’agroécologie (CCAE)
legal.d: Documented the Bt cotton withdrawal and follows the gene-drive mosquito programme. COPAGEN was created in 2004 at Grand-Bassam, headquartered in Côte d'Ivoire, and spans NINE COUNTRIES — the eight UEMOA states plus Guinea — with around TWO HUNDRED member organisations: farmer groups, unions, consumer associations and human rights movements. Its stated position is precise rather than blanket: yes to independent scientific research that values local biological resources and traditional knowledge in the interest of small farmers and consumers; no to PATENTING OF LIFE and to GMOs in agriculture and food. In Burkina Faso it works with the CCAE, and together they have carried two of the cases this map documents. THE BT COTTON FIELD STUDY: 'Le coton Bt et nous — la vérité de nos champs', researched 2014–16 and published 29 April 2017 with Inter Pares and CCFD-Terre Solidaire — farmer testimony rather than industry data, and the source for the figure of 47 billion CFA francs lost. AND THE GENE-DRIVE MOSQUITO RELEASE: they opposed the Target Malaria test release before the Agence nationale de biosécurité, argued it breached national and international law, and mobilised through customary and religious authorities, base communities and local elected officials. complain.n: ONSSA — Office National de Sécurité Sanitaire des Produits Alimentaires
complain.d: Handles food safety and labelling on imports. The food safety office; inspects and enforces. Created by loi n° 25-08 of 18 February 2009, an établissement public with legal personality and financial autonomy under the agriculture ministry, formed by REGROUPING the sanitary control functions previously scattered across several administrations. Food safety itself is governed by loi 28-07 of 11 February 2010. Its stated missions include the one that matters most here: it HOMOLOGATES AND CONTROLS AGRICULTURAL INPUTS — seeds, plant protection products and growing media — as well as veterinary medicines, alongside food safety across the whole chain including fish products and animal feed, and sanitary and phytosanitary risk assessment. It works through regional directorates and provincial services with its own veterinary, phytosanitary and food laboratories, and around 1,805 staff. Its legal base runs to more than 300 texts, consolidated on its own site — though only what is published in the Bulletin Officiel is authoritative.

legal.d: Works on seed law and farmer seed systems. The Moroccan agroecology networks, which also appear as the Réseau des initiatives agroécologiques au Maroc. Based in Rabat, and composed of INDIVIDUALS, COLLECTIVES AND AUTONOMOUS STRUCTURES rather than formal member organisations — so it is a meeting space for whoever is doing the work, which suits a country where much of it is small and dispersed. Its stated purposes are connecting agroecology actors through exchange of information and CAPITALISATION OF EXPERIENCE, giving initiatives visibility and common recognition, identifying resources for projects, and strengthening actors' skills. Its three cross-cutting aims name what this map cares about: contributing to COMMUNITY AUTONOMY, to FOOD SOVEREIGNTY and health, and to preserving natural heritage. For a reader in Morocco this is how to find the practitioners; ONSSA, named in this country's other entry, is the regulator. LINK CHECKED AND FOUND DEAD: the page or host no longer answers. complain.n: DSA de wilaya, avec la DPVCT et l’INPV (Algérie)
complain.d: Provincial agricultural services inspect. THE STRUCTURE IS THE USEFUL PART. Phytosanitary inspectors are SWORN AND COMMISSIONED AGENTS placed under the administrative authority of the DIRECTION DES SERVICES AGRICOLES OF THE WILAYA — so the office to approach is the wilaya, and the inspector who acts is an assermented officer. Nationally there are 48 phytosanitary inspections and 29 BORDER INSPECTIONS covering 12 maritime, 10 land and 7 air entry posts, with the INPV running 3 LABORATORIES and 4 anti-locust bases. The ministry's Direction de la Protection des Végétaux et des Contrôles Techniques writes the rules for production, import, export, distribution AND USE of agricultural inputs — SEEDS, PLANTS, VARIETIES, fertilisers and phytosanitary products — and for PLANT VARIETY PROTECTION, so seed and variety questions belong here. The INPV, created February 1975, controls agricultural products in international trade AND PLANTS AND SEEDS PRODUCED LOCALLY, treats outbreaks beyond farmers' capacity, and issues AVERTISSEMENTS AGRICOLES — preventive bulletins sent to growers through a wilaya-level comité de veille with the DSA and the chamber of agriculture. That warning system is a live channel a grower can be on.

complain.n: Direction du commerce — répression des fraudes
complain.d: Handles food labelling and fraud; Algeria prohibits engineered seed outright. Three things make this the practical route in Algeria. It operates under Law 09-03 on consumer protection and the suppression of fraud, whose article 35 provides for the fraud laboratories — run by the Centre Algérien du Contrôle de la Qualité et de l'Emballage, so this ministry has its own analytical capacity rather than depending on another's. Where a product is definitively withdrawn the trader must recall it from everywhere it is held, at the trader's own expense. And the administration can impose fixed fines without a court: 300,000 dinars for unsafe food, 300,000 for failure to carry out prior conformity checks, 200,000 for hygiene failures. decides.d: Handles approvals. Tunisia has no commercial cultivation; imported feed is the practical question. What the country profile actually holds: the national focal point and competent authorities the country has notified, its national biosafety law where filed, and the decisions it has submitted under Article 20. It is a country's OWN filings, so a thin profile means the country has filed little — not that it decides little. Filing is a treaty obligation without a sanction for missing it.

complain.n: Direction Générale de la Santé Végétale et du Contrôle des Intrants Agricoles (DGSVCIA)
complain.d: Plant health inspection. Its full title carries the useful half: it controls agricultural INPUTS — seed, pesticides, fungicides — including their certification and import, as well as plant health across the country. Seed is where an engineered organism enters, so the input-control mandate is the relevant one. The link goes to the IPPC country page because it carries the current named contact, address and phone; the directorate has no stable page of its own. Food on sale is a different route: Tunisia's 282 communes, with the health ministry's regional hygiene services, do the official control at the point of sale. The IPPC country page is the link here; the IPPC contacts entry in this box explains what that record gives and where it lags. Its attributions are wider than the IPPC entry shows: SEEDS AND PLANTS, pesticides, control of marketing, RESIDUE ANALYSIS, homologation, quarantine and plant disease campaigns, and locust, rodent and bird control. It has its own central Laboratoire de contrôle et d'analyse des pesticides in Tunis and THREE REGIONAL crop defence stations at Béja, Sousse and Sfax — so the complaint and the analysis are both here. It also holds the plant variety protection office, filing UPOV applications, at 30 rue Alain Savary, Tunis. And it PUBLISHES THE LIST OF PESTICIDES AUTHORISED IN TUNISIA on the national agricultural open-data catalogue, which is the link here — more useful to a reader than a contact page, because it says what may lawfully be applied.

complain.n: Institut National de la Consommation
complain.d: Handles food labelling complaints. Created 2008 under the trade ministry, it advises consumers, publishes comparative studies and — the part that matters here — carries out analyses and comparative tests on products through accredited or authorised laboratories, on its own initiative or at the request of public authorities or consumer organisations, and publishes the results. That is a route to a laboratory test that does not depend on owning the product's supply chain. Enforcement is elsewhere: the trade ministry's quality and consumer protection directorate takes complaints, inspects shops and can sanction.

certify.n: CTAB — Centre Technique de l’Agriculture Biologique
certify.d: The national organic technical centre. It publishes the list of control and certification bodies approved in Tunisia for organic agriculture, which is the useful page: the centre itself does not certify. Note also that it holds an organic certificate for its own experimental plot at Chott Mariem, contracted with a control body since 2002, and receives that body's inspection visits — the national technical centre for organic agriculture is itself inspected like any other operator. Two addresses circulate for it, ctab.tn and ctab.nat.tn; the first is the one that answers.

decides.d: Serbia prohibits the cultivation and trade of engineered crops under its GMO law, which has been a live issue in its EU accession talks because the prohibition is stricter than EU law permits.

complain.n: Phytosanitary inspection — Ministry of Agriculture (Serbia)
complain.d: Inspects seed and crops. One caution about this source: the IPPC contact record is updated by the country itself and can lag — records checked here carried ministry names that had since changed. The named person, address and telephone are the useful part; treat the institutional name as a starting point and check it against the ministry's own site. Serbia's inspection work is split across the ministry's sectors, and this file already names the agricultural inspectorate separately — the one whose remit is the LAND rather than the product, with departments for land use, cultivation, soil fertility testing and organic production. The phytosanitary side handles plant health, seed and planting material, and plant protection products. Which of the two a reader wants depends on whether the question is about the field or about what was applied to it. Consumer complaints run separately again, through the trade ministry, which forwards them to whichever inspection is competent.

complain.n: Ministry of Agriculture — food inspection
complain.d: Handles labelling; Serbian law prohibits cultivation and trade, so what is on a shelf is the question. The agriculture inspection sector of the ministry, based in Novi Beograd, supervises the use of agricultural land, its regular cultivation, changes of land use, soil fertility testing and organic production, with a department for each. That matters for a contamination question: an inspectorate whose remit is the land rather than the product is the one that can look at a field. Consumer complaints are a separate route again — the trade ministry runs the consumer protection framework, and complaints alleging a breach are forwarded to whichever inspection is competent. The ZAKON O BEZBEDNOSTI HRANE (Food Safety Law) divides competence by PRODUCT AND STAGE, which is why routing matters: food of PLANT ORIGIN is the FITOSANITARNA INSPEKCIJA at every stage — primary production, import, transit and export; food of animal origin is the veterinary inspection; processing and wholesale of plant-origin food and non-alcoholic drinks is the agricultural inspection; mixed foods draw both; and the health ministry's sanitary inspection covers retail. THE CONSUMER-FACING POINT: complaints about the quality of PLANTING MATERIAL — seed and fruit saplings — and about ANIMAL FEED are expressly the phytosanitary inspection's business, and it sits in the Uprava za zaštitu bilja with internal and border arms and CONTACT DETAILS PUBLISHED BY DISTRICT, so a reader can reach the nearest office. Serbia states zero tolerance for GMO cultivation and trade, though article 5 of the Food Safety Law lists GM food and GM feed as categories, which was publicly contested when the law passed. Border control is reported to check only 4–7% of imported consignments.

Search it by country of operation rather than by country of origin: in most places the certificate a grower actually holds is issued by a multinational certifier working locally, not by a body founded there, and the national names in this category are only part of the picture.

complain.n: ГГИСКЗР — Main State Inspectorate for Seed Breeding, Quarantine and Plant Protection (Belarus)
complain.d: Inspects seed. THE FULL NAME MATTERS because it shows the scope: SEED BREEDING, QUARANTINE AND PLANT PROTECTION IN ONE INSPECTORATE, under the Ministry of Agriculture and Food. So seed certification, phytosanitary quarantine and the REGISTRATION OF PLANT PROTECTION PRODUCTS AND FERTILISERS are all handled at the same address — it has a dedicated Otdel registratsii SZR (plant protection product registration department) which publishes its own payment details, and a Department of Quarantine Phytosanitary Expertise and Methodological Work. That expertise department is the one to ask for a determination. 220034, Minsk, Krasnozvjozdnaja str. 8. Two notes: state registration of a plant protection product or fertiliser carries a fee set against the national BASE VALUE, and the payment must name the trade name of the product — so the register is traceable product by product; and one of the inspectorate's laboratory accreditation certificates is recorded as WITHDRAWN following the expiry of a suspension, so confirm current accreditation before relying on a test result.

complain.n: Gosstandart — consumer protection
complain.d: Handles labelling; Belarus requires GM labelling and runs a fuller BCH node than most in the region. The State Committee for Standardization, operating under the Council of Ministers, with more than 430 food standards and over 2,400 across all industries. Note where the rules actually come from: it states that its standards form the basis for safety requirements applied under Eurasian Economic Union technical regulation, so the binding rule for a product in Belarus is often a union-level one rather than a purely national one — the same relationship EU member states have with EU regulation.

decides.d: Handles biosafety. Kazakhstan has a BSL4 laboratory and a substantial biological research sector, so containment rather than cultivation is the live question here. The Clearing-House entry in this box explains what a country profile holds and what a thin one means.

complain.n: Committee of State Inspection in the Agro-Industrial Complex — Ministry of Agriculture (Kazakhstan)
complain.d: Inspects seed and imports. The unit to name is the COMMITTEE OF STATE INSPECTION IN THE AGRO-INDUSTRIAL COMPLEX, constituted by MINISTERIAL ORDER No. 221 of 1 June 2017. It holds PLANT PROTECTION AND QUARANTINE together with SEED AND GRAIN MARKET REGULATION and crop production, appoints the CHIEF STATE PLANT QUARANTINE INSPECTOR and sets the qualification requirements for state quarantine inspectors. Crucially it works through DISTRICT-LEVEL TERRITORIAL INSPECTIONS, each a separate public institution — so the office to approach is the territorial inspection for the district, not Astana. Note the districts have been renamed and subdivided repeatedly by government order, so verify the current name. A candid finding: in 2024 Russia's Rosselkhoznadzor accused Kazakhstan over the quality of phytosanitary certificates used to re-export flowers; the Committee rejected the accusation BUT ACKNOWLEDGED A PROBLEM WITH COMPANIES REGISTERING QUARANTINE PRODUCTS TO SHELL COMPANIES WHEN OBTAINING PHYTOSANITARY CERTIFICATES — so a certificate here may not identify the real consignor. Risk assessment is shared with the health ministry's Committee for Public Health Protection and the Committee for Veterinary Control.

complain.n: Consumer protection — Ministry of Trade and Integration (Kazakhstan)
complain.d: Handles food labelling complaints. Consumer protection moved here when the ministry was created in June 2019, taking that function from the national economy ministry and technical regulation and standardisation from the industry ministry. So the body that handles a consumer complaint and the body that sets the technical standard are now the same ministry — worth knowing, and worth checking, because functions in Kazakhstan have moved between ministries more than once.

Slovakia's other authorised body is Czech. Between them they cover crop and livestock production, seed and propagating material, wild collection, mushrooms, beekeeping, processing, wine, and import and export to and from third countries.

Handles the cultivation register; most Latvian municipalities have declared themselves GM-free.

complain.n: Pārtikas un veterinārais dienests (PVD) — Food and Veterinary Service
complain.d: Operating under the agriculture ministry since 1 January 2002 on a stated 'from field to table' surveillance concept, which is the useful part: the service traces the whole production cycle rather than only the product on sale, so a field problem and a shelf problem reach the same body. Eleven regional boards do the actual surveillance and inspection work — the central office in Riga does strategy and method, so a complaint goes to the regional board. Testing is separate: BIOR, the Institute of Food Safety, Animal Health and Environment, does the laboratory work. On GM specifically, Latvia divides the work four ways and the agriculture ministry states it plainly: PVD SUPERVISES AND CONTROLS GM FOOD AND FEED IN CIRCULATION; BIOR is the competent institution for GMO RISK ASSESSMENT and for issuing authorisations for GMO activities; and the STATE PLANT PROTECTION SERVICE (VAAD) is responsible for GMO supervision and control IN SEED AND PLANT PROPAGATING MATERIAL and for overseeing compliance with COEXISTENCE conditions — the law empowers VAAD to take seed and propagating-material samples to check for GMO presence. So seed goes to VAAD, food and feed to PVD, the authorisation to BIOR. Within PVD, evaluation of specific foods before they reach the market — supplements, dietetic food, GMOs and novel foods — sits with the Food Surveillance Department, and border inspectors at roads, ports, rail, post, the airport and customs warehouses check documents against cargo and TAKE SAMPLES for laboratory examination. Labelling follows EU Regulation 1830/2003, with the 0.9% threshold for accidental or technically unavoidable presence — and the operator must be able to prove to the authorities that it acted to avoid it.

complain.n: Põllumajandus- ja Toiduamet (PTA) — Agriculture and Food Board
complain.d: Created 1 January 2021 by merging the Agricultural Board with the Veterinary and Food Board, so anything citing either separately predates the merger. It supervises the whole food chain and its remit names the relevant work outright: plant protection, plant health, plant variety rights, seed and propagating material, organic farming, and the HANDLING OF GENETICALLY MODIFIED CROPS. Testing is a different body again — LABRIS, the National Centre for Laboratory Research and Risk Assessment, does the diagnostic and quality analysis that supports PTA's enforcement.
