test.d: The sub-regional laboratory for analysis of pesticides and pesticide residues in food in Central Africa, run under CEMAC. Its Biology Department carries an OGM/mycotoxins sector alongside veterinary, bacteriology, virology and biopesticides work, so detection capacity for engineered material exists here as one department of an institution built primarily for residue analysis rather than as a dedicated GMO laboratory. Accreditation across the sub-region is the weak point: the CEMAC and CEEAC laboratory mapping carried out under the EU-funded PACIE programme covered 47 testing laboratories in seven countries and found good technical competence but a general need for support to reach ISO/IEC 17025, so a result may not carry formal recognition. Samples otherwise go to Cameroon's national laboratories rather than to West Africa. nearest capable laboratory is in another country and access runs through the regional body.

fe_register.d: The regional federation, which sets standards and runs training where no statutory regulator exists. Most African fertility care is private and unlicensed, so a professional body is often the only body holding standards. One point applies to every professional register in this category: it is not a licence. A clinic missing from it may simply not have joined, and a clinic in it has met a society's conditions rather than a state's. Where a country has no statutory regulator, this is the best record available and also not a register of who is permitted to practise.

fe_register.n: ANARA — African Network and Registry for ART
fe_register.d: Collects cycle-by-cycle data from the ART centres that choose to submit it and publishes procedure counts, pregnancy and delivery rates and centre numbers by country. Reporting is voluntary and centre-led, so a country showing nothing may have clinics that have never submitted rather than no clinics. It does not license a clinic, inspect one, or take a complaint about one. One point applies to every professional register in this category: it is not a licence. A clinic missing from it may simply not have joined, and a clinic in it has met a society's conditions rather than a state's. Where a country has no statutory regulator, this is the best record available and also not a register of who is permitted to practise.

decides.d: Handles approvals. Côte d’Ivoire has a BSL4 laboratory under construction — one of only three high-containment facilities in Africa — while scoring among the lowest on biorisk governance of any country with one. complain.n: DPVCQ — Direction de la Protection des Végétaux, du Contrôle et de la Qualité (Côte d’Ivoire)
complain.d: Inspects and enforces. The DPVCQ sits in the Direction Générale des Productions et de la Sécurité Alimentaire and ALSO HOSTS THE PERMANENT SECRETARIAT OF THE PESTICIDES COMMITTEE — so registration, distributor approval and phytosanitary control are at one address: Immeuble CAISTAB, 14th floor, Abidjan-Plateau, 01 BP 12243. Import of pesticides runs through the GUCE single window, generating a PRELIMINARY IMPORT AUTHORISATION sent to the DPVCQ, under Décret n°89.02 of 4 January 1989; a PESTICIDE DISTRIBUTOR APPROVAL is required and may be granted to any natural or legal person WITHOUT RESTRICTION OF NATIONALITY. Seeds are a SEPARATE DIRECTORATE: the DIRECTION DES SEMENCES, ENGRAIS ET PRODUITS ASSIMILÉS handles seed and fertiliser regulation, VARIETY HOMOLOGATION with the research institutes, and SEED QUALITY CONTROL AND CERTIFICATION — so a seed question goes there, not to the DPVCQ.

complain.n: CODINORM
complain.d: Draws up and publishes Ivorian standards and runs the national product certification mark, including the labelling standards a packaged food is sold under. It is a non-profit association of member firms and the State rather than a ministry, so it sets and certifies against standards; enforcement against a seller sits elsewhere.

The sub-regional network it anchors is still being formed, so this is the designated route rather than a demonstrated routine one and a sample crossing a border may have to be arranged case by case; detection capacity in the region in practice sits in Nigeria, Ghana and Burkina Faso. It analyses a sample and reports; it does not authorise a release and does not take a complaint. nearest capable laboratory is in another country and access runs through the regional body. complain.d: A CORRECTION. The former Institut Sénégalais de Normalisation became the ASSOCIATION Sénégalaise de Normalisation by decree 2002-746 of 19 July 2002, supervised by the industry ministry. Its stated mission is identifying standards requirements and developing national standards, product and system CERTIFICATION, promoting quality, and representing Senegal in regional and international standardisation bodies. Enforcement is not among them. So this is a standards and certification body, not a complaints route — for a field or food problem the agriculture ministry's Direction de la Protection des Végétaux, named in the IPPC register, is the address.

complain.n: OPV — Office de Protection des Végétaux (Mali)
complain.d: Inspects and enforces. One caution about this source: the IPPC contact record is updated by the country itself and can lag — records checked here carried ministry names that had since changed. The named person, address and telephone are the useful part; treat the institutional name as a starting point and check it against the ministry's own site. Created by Loi N°05-011 of 11 February 2005, which repealed the 1996 law establishing the Direction Nationale de l'Appui au Monde Rural. Its statutory mission is to implement national plant protection policy: coordinating surveillance of plants and crops to report the existence, appearance and spread of plant enemies; taking and coordinating control measures; DISINFESTING OR DISINFECTING consignments of plants and plant products in international trade; and developing and extending alternative control methods. Governed by a board, a directorate general and a management committee. One thing a reader should expect, from the OPV's own board proceedings: it has operated with roughly a third of its established staffing — 124 agents against an organic framework of 303 — while also carrying forest and natural-space protection duties. Quartier du Fleuve, Bamako; the IPPC page carries the named contact and telephone.

legal.d: The national farmers' coordination, in one of the few regional liability protocol parties. LA VÍA CAMPESINA'S MEMBER IN MALI, and the peasant coordination behind the country's food sovereignty framework. A caution on the name: CNOP IS USED BY SEVERAL COUNTRIES — Mali's Coordination Nationale, plus separate CNOP bodies in Congo, Cameroon and Guinea — so name the country when searching. Its own domain, cnop-mali.org, has been intermittent; the La Vía Campesina member page linked here is the stable route to its current contacts. complain.n: DSV — Departamento de Sanidade Vegetal, Ministério da Agricultura (Moçambique)
complain.d: Inspects seed and imports. The DSV is Mozambique's national plant protection organisation and holds PLANT QUARANTINE, PESTICIDE REGISTRATION AND CONTROL, and pest management TOGETHER — so an input complaint and a plant health complaint share one address. The legal base is the REGULAMENTO DE INSPECÇÃO FITOSSANITÁRIA E QUARENTENA VEGETAL, DECRETO nº 5/2009 of 1 June. It inspects, issues licences and phytosanitary certificates on import and export, monitors and diagnoses pests, trains technicians in plant protection and implements IPM programmes. Mozambique is a member of IRLCO-CSA for MIGRATORY PEST control. Two candid figures: the ministry estimates production losses of AROUND 40% where control measures are not applied in time; and an IPPC capacity evaluation records that the government funds allocated annually to the NPPO ARE NOT SUFFICIENT to fulfil its mission.

complain.n: INNOQ — Instituto Nacional de Normalização e Qualidade (Moçambique)
complain.d: Handles labelling standards. Created 24 March 1993 by Law Decree 02/93 and now governed by DECRETO 81/2020 of 9 September, under the MINISTRY OF INDUSTRY AND TRADE since 2000 — an autonomous public institute covering standardisation, metrology, CERTIFICATION and quality management, with consumer AND ENVIRONMENTAL protection among its stated aims. It develops technical standards for food products and provides certification verifying compliance. Av. de Moçambique, Parcela 7168/D1/7, Bairro Zimpeto, Maputo. Note the boundary: PLANT HEALTH, PESTICIDE REGISTRATION AND QUARANTINE ARE NOT HERE — they sit with the DEPARTAMENTO DE SANIDADE VEGETAL of the agriculture ministry.

legal.d: Files on agricultural and environmental decisions and works on seed law.

The national peasants' union, which represents growers on seed law and the drought-tolerant maize trials. Founded April 1987 and registered 1994, formed by peasants themselves at a moment of forced transition — the shift from a centrally planned economy to a market one under IMF and World Bank adhesion — which is why its founding concern was what would become of the cooperatives without state support. It is LA VÍA CAMPESINA'S MEMBER IN MOZAMBIQUE, organised through PROVINCIAL UNIONS across the country, so it reaches beyond Maputo. Its published commitments name the things this map tracks: access to and control of LAND by peasants, DEFENCE OF THE COMMONS — water, SEEDS, environment, biodiversity — active peasant participation in policy definition, and development of local markets. It is the standing counterpart to LAND ACQUISITION for export production, which its own material treats under the term usurpation. Rua da Resistência 1803, Maputo; it publishes a regular bulletin.

decides.d: Authorises. Malawi approved Bt cotton for commercial planting in 2018, one of the few African countries to do so, and is a party to the Nagoya–Kuala Lumpur liability protocol. The Clearing-House entry in this box explains what a country profile holds and what a thin one means.

complain.n: Ministry of Agriculture and its Agricultural Development Divisions (Malawi)
complain.d: Inspects seed and crops. A LIMIT WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU REPORT: the AGRICULTURAL DEVELOPMENT DIVISIONS (ADDs), the ministry's regional arms, CAN CHECK AND REPORT ILLEGALLY USED PESTICIDES BUT CANNOT IMPOUND THEM — so a report to an ADD starts a process, it does not stop the use. Malawi's own assessment states plainly that with limited resources GOVERNMENT DOES NOT HAVE THE CAPACITY TO FULLY REGULATE PESTICIDE USE. MALAWI MANUFACTURES NO PESTICIDES — all are imported — with insecticides most used, herbicides concentrated in sugar plantations, FUMIGANTS DOMINANT IN THE TOBACCO INDUSTRY, and insecticides mostly on field crops, particularly maize. BOTANICALS are also in use. Read with this country's other entries: MBS enforces standards by gazette order, CISANET is the policy route, and MOGA and SFHC work with organic growers.

complain.n: MBS — Malawi Bureau of Standards
complain.d: Handles food labelling standards and complaints. Statutory body established 1972 (Cap 51:02, amended by Act No. 14 of 2012). It DOES enforce, and the Act says how: on the Board's recommendation the Minister may declare a Malawi Standard MANDATORY by order in the Gazette, after which no person may manufacture or sell a commodity to which it applies except in accordance with it, and a manufacturer must obtain the Bureau's permission before starting to make a commodity covered by a mandatory standard. Its Quality Assurance Services Department implements standards through inspection and certification, and a separate Testing Services Department does product and sample testing — so the complaint and the analysis are both here. It also runs an Imports Quality Monitoring Scheme, established 1993. Note the domain: mbsmw.org, not mbs.mw.

certify.d: Groundnut and coffee for export. Search it by country of operation rather than by country of origin: in most places the certificate a grower actually holds is issued by a multinational certifier working locally, not by a body founded there, and the national names in this category are only part of the picture.

legal.d: Represents smallholder growers on the Bt cotton approval and seed law. Incorporated under the Trustees Incorporation Act 1964 on 23 January 2005, it is a NETWORK that exists specifically to give non-state actors a way to engage government on agricultural POLICY — so it is the route for a rule or a programme rather than an individual grievance. Two of its programmes matter here: work on the RIGHT TO FOOD through strengthening local governance, and a transparency and accountability project on Malawi's AFFORDABLE INPUTS PROGRAMME, the state subsidy through which seed and fertiliser reach smallholders — which is the mechanism a reader would need to understand to know what seed is being distributed and on whose terms. It works with members at both NATIONAL AND DISTRICT level. Lilongwe. LINK CHECKED AND FOUND DEAD: the page or host no longer answers. The body may well still exist — government sites move and rename constantly — so confirm through the worldwide routes in this box, or the Biosafety Clearing-House or IPPC contact page for this country, rather than treating the absence as evidence the body has gone.

legal.n: MOGA — Malawi Organic Growers Association (and SFHC)
legal.d: Represents growers in a country that approved Bt cotton and is a liability protocol party. MOGA was registered in 2000 and reports OVER 37,000 REGISTERED MEMBERS — producers, processors, traders and researchers — which makes it one of the larger membership bodies in this file. Beside it, SOILS, FOOD AND HEALTHY COMMUNITIES (SFHC) works with over 6,000 smallholder farmers on FARMER-LED EXPERIMENTATION, indigenous crops and knowledge sharing. The practical mechanism worth carrying: cooperative projects in Malawi have established GROUP CERTIFICATION for smallholders and trained INTERNAL CO-OPERATIVE INSPECTORS — farmers inspecting each other's compliance so the cost of certification is shared rather than borne per farm, alongside Village Savings and Loans Associations. That is the same answer to certification cost as Belgium's participatory guarantee system, reached independently. Note MOGA's own web presence is thin; the listing linked here is a stable directory record. Read with CISANET, this country's policy route.

decides.d: Authorises under the Biosafety Act. Namibia requires labelling of GM food and its rules are among the more developed in southern Africa outside South Africa.

complain.n: Plant Quarantine Division — Ministry of Agriculture (Namibia)
complain.d: Inspects imports and seed. The unit is the PLANT QUARANTINE DIVISION and the instrument is the PLANT QUARANTINE ACT, whose procedures publish the address in full: by post to the Director: Plant Quarantine Division, Private Bag 13184, Windhoek; BY HAND at the corner of Peter Muller Street and Robert Mugabe Avenue, Windhoek. An application to import regulated goods must be submitted IN TRIPLICATE AT LEAST 30 DAYS BEFORE ARRIVAL, and for a plant, plant product, PATHOGEN, INSECT OR EXOTIC ANIMAL the COMMON AND SCIENTIFIC NAMES must both be specified — so the permit record identifies exactly what was brought in. Seized items carry an identification mark or seal bearing THE DATE OF SEIZURE AND A SERIAL NUMBER, which makes a seizure traceable. Note the ministry has been renamed — Agriculture, Water and Land Reform in recent usage, Agriculture, Water and Forestry in older citations.

complain.n: NSI — Namibian Standards Institution
complain.d: A CAUTION on this one. NSI is established under the Standards Act 18 of 2005 and governed by the Namibian Standards Council, inaugurated February 2011. Its published functions are the National Quality Policy, developing and publishing Namibian standards to WTO requirements, training, metrology traceability, and testing — and the testing it names is MAINLY ON FISH AND FISHERY PRODUCTS, shellfish, potable water, sea water and wastes, for the aquaculture and fishing industries, through its chemistry and microbiology laboratories. Enforcement is not among the stated functions, and neither is crop or general food inspection. So for a fisheries or water question this is the laboratory; for anything growing in a field it is likely the wrong door, and the agriculture ministry's plant health services are the address to look for.

complain.n: Department of Plant Health — NPPO of Botswana
complain.d: Inspects imports. The unit is the DEPARTMENT OF PLANT HEALTH, Botswana's national plant protection organisation, Private Bag 0091, Gaborone; IPPC contact registered September 2023, so the named director should hold. Read with this country's other entry: BOBS enforces on SEVEN COMPULSORY PRODUCTS INCLUDING ANIMAL FEED AND GRAIN, so a feed or grain complaint has a second address.

complain.n: BOBS — Botswana Bureau of Standards
complain.d: Writes Botswana's national standards and enforces the compulsory ones, which include cereals and grains for consumption and cattle and poultry feed — the products an engineered crop arrives in. It certifies against a standard and runs the testing laboratories; it does not authorise a release, and a compulsory standard is a trade requirement rather than a biosafety decision. It enforces, and the scope is narrow enough to be worth knowing exactly. A parastatal since April 1997 under the Standards Act 1995, governed by a 12-member Standards Council. Botswana's regime splits into voluntary and COMPULSORY standards, and only the second are enforceable: violating one is an offence under section 13, carrying up to three years' imprisonment and a fine under section 14. Compulsory standards cover SEVEN product groups — petroleum gas, poultry feed, pre-packaged consumer goods, cereals and sorghum grains for consumption, cattle feed, garments, and drinking water. FEED AND GRAIN ARE ON THAT LIST, which is what makes BOBS relevant here; anything outside the seven falls under a voluntary standard with no enforcement behind it. The Compulsory Standards Regulation was gazetted 23 June 2023 and took effect 1 April 2024, requiring local manufacturers of regulated products to register with the Bureau. No waivers are available. Note the domain moved to bobstandards.bw from bobs.co.bw.

complain.n: RICA — Rwanda Inspectorate, Competition and Consumer Protection Authority
complain.d: Inspects seed and crops. A CORRECTION ON THE ADDRESS: inspection and enforcement sit with RICA, not the Rwanda Agriculture Board (RAB), which is a research and development body. RICA was established by LAW Nº 31/2017 of 25/07/2017 and inspects, registers and licenses SEEDS, SEEDLINGS, CUTTINGS, agrochemicals, plant pharmaceutical products, fertilisers, animal feed, SEMEN AND FERTILISED EGGS — that last pair is rare in this file and covers animal genetic material directly. It also oversees LABELLING, PACKAGING AND ADVERTISING, so a mislabelled product is squarely within its mandate. Its structure is published down to post level: a Farm Products and Processes Inspection Unit of 25 including TEN SEED INSPECTORS and four agrochemical product and premises inspectors, and a Registration and Licensing Unit with a dedicated Plant & Seeds Registration Officer. AND IT PUBLISHES A REGISTER OF LICENSED BUSINESS OPERATORS — a November 2022 edition listed 448 seed producers and 413 agrochemical dealers by name, under a Unique Numbering System — so a reader can check whether a dealer is licensed at all. Kigali; info@rica.gov.rw. Note this RICA is distinct from the Rwanda Institute for Conservation Agriculture, a university.

complain.n: RSB — Rwanda Standards Board
complain.d: A CORRECTION worth reading before writing to it. RSB was created from the Rwanda Bureau of Standards by Law N° 50/2013, and the 2013 restructuring MOVED THE ENFORCEMENT FUNCTIONS OUT — standards inspections and legal metrology verification went to a separate independent body. RSB is now a service provider: it develops and publishes national standards, over 4,130 of them covering food and agriculture among other fields, certifies products and systems, runs testing and calibration laboratories, and provides metrology services. So it is the right address for a TEST and the wrong one for an enforcement complaint. One power it does retain at the border: an imported product related to health, safety or environment needs an RSB officer to authorise release through the single electronic window, and RSB can carry out quality checks at the owner's premises. Proposed technical regulations are published for comment for 30 to 90 days, with final regulations in the official gazette.

test.n: KEPHIS — Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Service
test.d: Kenya's plant health regulator and designated National Plant Protection Organization, whose plant quarantine section is the regional reference laboratory for COMESA and a centre of excellence for germplasm exchange, so it accepts samples from neighbouring states. Its laboratories cover molecular diagnosis by conventional and real-time PCR and LAMP, bacteriology, virology, analytical chemistry and seed testing, and it takes samples from farmers directly as well as from its own inspectors; the bacteriology laboratory is ISO/IEC 17025 accredited. It analyses and inspects: it does not authorise a GMO. Importing one is approved by Kenya's National Biosafety Authority, and KEPHIS issues the permit only after that approval. nearest capable laboratory is in another country and access runs through the regional body.

decides.d: Handles biosafety. Jordan imports nearly all its grain, and its labelling requirements are the practical point for a consumer. The Clearing-House entry in this box explains what a country profile holds and what a thin one means.

complain.n: Jordan Food and Drug Administration
complain.d: Handles food labelling and safety complaints. Created 2003 as the SOLE national competent authority for both food safety and quality and drug safety and efficacy — an independent public regulator rather than a directorate inside a ministry. That single-authority structure is unusual on this map, where the same job is normally split across an agriculture ministry, a health ministry and a standards body. Its remit covers labelling as well as safety, and it inspects foodstuffs against the technical rules and standards in force. On GM specifically, which is why this row exists: the JFDA has a DEPARTMENT OF BIOSAFETY OF FOOD responsible for the safety of GMO foods and their products, under Law No. 41 of 2008. Jordan prohibits importing crops expressing engineered traits INTENDED FOR CULTIVATION OR RELEASE, and prohibits marketing food containing unapproved traits not authorised by the Jordanian National Biosafety and Biosecurity Committee. Before 2020 the JFDA barred imports of engineered crops and derived raw materials outright; the GE HANDLING INSTRUCTIONS published in the Official Gazette on 3 April 2020 changed that — importers of products labelled as possibly containing engineered ingredients can now register those products with the JFDA in advance. Expect detentions: the JFDA is reported to detain and destroy imported consumer food found carrying unregistered engineered content. Three ministries share the wider field — agriculture, environment (which enacted a 2016 biosafety law requiring labelling) and the JFDA, which aims to hold sole oversight of engineered food. Health Regulation No. 29 of 2019 established a National Committee on Biosafety on the Cartagena model.

complain.n: National Food Agency (Georgia) — სურსათის ეროვნული სააგენტო
complain.d: Handles labelling; Georgia requires GM labelling. Inspects food, feed and seed. Under the environmental protection and agriculture ministry, with a hotline on 1501 and regional offices across the country, each with a named contact. Its structure puts the relevant work in one agency: a plant protection department covering phytosanitary monitoring, plant quarantine and the registration of plant protection and agrochemical products, alongside a food safety department. It runs state monitoring programmes that sample from retail and test at an accredited laboratory. Note for searching: “Georgia consumer complaint” returns the US state's attorney general almost exclusively; the country's agency is nfa.gov.ge. A legal entity of public law under the MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND AGRICULTURE — note environment and agriculture are one ministry here — consolidating food safety, veterinary control, PLANT QUARANTINE and export certification in a single agency. Its structure names the units to write to: a PLANT PROTECTION DEPARTMENT with divisions for phytosanitary monitoring, REGISTRATION OF PLANT PROTECTION AND AGROCHEMICAL PRODUCTS, plant quarantine, control and recognition of those products, and plant health; and a FOOD SAFETY DEPARTMENT with divisions for food of animal and NON-ANIMAL origin, food trade and catering, and certification. So the pesticide register and the food complaint are in one agency, with regional offices and a HOTLINE, 1501. It performs residue testing and issues export certification. Its published enforcement includes identifying UNREGISTERED OUTLETS SELLING PLANT PROTECTION PRODUCTS. Its legislation page separates government acts on food safety, veterinary medicine and PLANT PROTECTION, plus orders of the agency head.

test.n: EAEU accredited laboratories — conformity testing route
test.d: Armenia has been a member of the Eurasian Economic Union since January 2015, alongside Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, and conformity testing under the union's technical regulations is carried out in laboratories accredited in any member state with the result recognised across all five. That is the mechanism behind detection capacity sitting in the larger members rather than at home. Two limits are worth knowing before relying on it. It is a TRADE conformity route, built for placing a product on the market, not a public testing service a grower or a neighbour can simply send a field sample to. And no laboratory in the union was identified as a designated reference laboratory for detecting engineered material specifically; the reference facilities that surfaced in Kazakhstan are for dangerous human and animal pathogens, which is a different discipline from finding a transgene in seed. nearest capable laboratory is in another country and access runs through the regional body.

complain.n: AKU — Autoriteti Kombëtar i Ushqimit
complain.d: Inspects food and imports, under the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, and it takes reports from the public through a free green line, an official e-mail address, its social accounts and a “Denonco” form on its own site. That route is counted rather than nominal: in 2019 it recorded 175 citizen reports received through those channels and answered, alongside 29,206 planned field inspections. The border is where its weight sits — the same year it carried out 68,245 checks at border inspection points, more than double its inland inspections, which matters in a country that prohibits cultivation of engineered crops and so meets them as imports rather than as plantings. It acts on food as it arrives and as it is sold; the release decision is the environment ministry's.

decides.n: Council of Ministers — Food Safety Agency
decides.d: Holds biosafety, split across the entities, which makes a single national answer difficult. The Agency was set up under the 2004 Law on Food and became fully operational in 2006 as part of harmonising with EU law and Codex. It ran a TAIEX expert mission in December 2019 to analyse the country's legislation on genetically modified organisms, which is the clearest public account of where that law stands.

complain.n: FSA BiH — Food Safety Agency of Bosnia and Herzegovina
complain.d: An independent state-level administrative organisation doing scientific risk assessment and expert opinion on food and animal feed, running the rapid alert system and the INFOSAN contact point, and coordinating with EFSA. It does NOT inspect: official controls at import and on the market are carried out by the competent inspection bodies, which sit at entity level, so a complaint about a specific sample goes to an entity inspectorate and not to Mostar. The state-level agency, and a reader should expect the constitutional structure to matter more here than almost anywhere in this file. Alongside the FSA and the state Veterinary Office, competence is held by the Ministry of Agriculture, Water Management and Forestry of the FEDERATION, the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management of REPUBLIKA SRPSKA, and the Department for Agriculture of BRČKO DISTRICT — with inspection carried out by three separate bodies again: the Federal Administration for Inspection Affairs, the Republic Administration for Inspection Affairs, and the Brčko Inspectorate. So the state agency coordinates and manages risk, while the inspector who would visit a premises answers to an entity or the district. Which one depends on where the premises is. The FSA holds a Department for Risk Management, Emergencies and Traceability, which is the state-level function to approach.

complain.n: FVA — Food and Veterinary Agency (North Macedonia)
complain.d: An independent body of the government holding food and animal-feed safety, veterinary supervision, and control of the national reference and authorised laboratories. It is the country's contact point for EFSA, the EU rapid alert system and Codex, so a finding reported here travels beyond the country. It inspects what is on the market and in transit; it does not authorise a release. An INDEPENDENT body of the government, not a ministry directorate, competent under article 119 of the Law on Food Safety to coordinate legislation and control systems across the institutions and to communicate with the EU. Its GMO position is stated precisely: THREE bodies share the field — the Ministry of Environment and Physical Planning adopted the Law on GMOs in 2008 and holds the release side, the agriculture ministry has primary production through the State Agricultural Inspectorate and the Phytosanitary Directorate, and the FVA IS RESPONSIBLE FOR GMO FOOD AND FEED, including the rulebooks on labelling and traceability of food containing or produced from GMOs. So a labelling complaint comes here; a release question goes to the environment ministry. It is also the contact point for EFSA, RASFF and Codex, with an INFOSAN emergency contact, and it controls the national reference laboratories. Regional offices in Skopje, Strumica, Bitola and Prilep among others.

complain.n: UBHVFP — Administration for Food Safety, Veterinary and Phytosanitary Affairs
complain.d: Holds food safety, veterinary and phytosanitary inspection, and runs a standing consumers' channel through which a member of the public can put a question or an initiative directly to its inspectors. It acts on food and on plant and animal consignments; a release decision is taken elsewhere. The competent authority for implementing legislation and carrying out official controls across food and feed safety, veterinary and phytosanitary affairs, under the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management, and it performs administrative, regulatory, INSPECTION and expert tasks itself. Its published topic list names BIOTECHNOLOGY AND GENETIC ENGINEERING alongside plant health, plant protection products, contaminants, novel foods and feed — so an engineered-organism question is explicitly inside its remit rather than referred elsewhere. It is Montenegro's EFSA focal point and its WOAH delegate. Serdara Jola Piletića 26, Podgorica. Note the English name is rendered both Administration and Directorate on official pages.

complain.n: Plant Protection Directorate — Ministry of Agriculture (Iraq)
complain.d: Inspects imports and seed. Iraq's IPPC contact is registered to a Director General within the agriculture ministry, contact registration DECEMBER 2024, Arabic-preferred — so correspondence should be in Arabic. Read with this country's other entry: COSQC under the PLANNING ministry holds standards, quality control laboratories and, together with the MINISTRY OF HEALTH, is named by FAO as Iraq's competent authority on GM food. So there are THREE ministries in play — agriculture for plant health, planning for standards, health for food — and a GM question should be addressed to COSQC and Health rather than here.

complain.n: COSQC — Central Organization for Standardization and Quality Control (Iraq)
complain.d: Handles food labelling standards. Established by LAW No. 54 of 1979 and sitting under the MINISTRY OF PLANNING rather than agriculture or health — an unusual placement, so a complaint about a product's composition is a planning-ministry matter here. Its Directorate of Quality Control includes a FOOD INDUSTRIES DEPARTMENT and a CHEMICAL INDUSTRIES DEPARTMENT, and it runs quality control laboratories, a number of them ACCREDITED TO ISO 17025 by the Iraqi Accreditation Commission since 2016 — so there is testing capacity with a recognised standard behind it. On GM food specifically, FAO's platform names COSQC together with the MINISTRY OF HEALTH as the competent authorities for Iraq, so both should be addressed. Two operational notes: the Cabinet has directed COSQC, WITH THE DIRECTORATE FOR COMBATING ORGANIZED CRIME, to monitor UNLICENSED FACTORIES and pursue their owners; and inspection and compliance certification for imported goods has been contracted to external companies, so a border decision may be made by a private inspector rather than the organisation itself. P.O. Box 13032, Al-Jaderiya, Baghdad.

complain.n: PPO — Plant Protection Organization (سازمان حفظ نباتات)
complain.d: Inspects seed and crops. One caution about this source: the IPPC contact record is updated by the country itself and can lag — records checked here carried ministry names that had since changed. The named person, address and telephone are the useful part; treat the institutional name as a starting point and check it against the ministry's own site. Its powers under the Plant Protection Act are unusually hard-edged and worth knowing before writing to it. The Act lets the PPO order control measures and, where an owner refuses to comply, requires THE POLICE FORCE to assist plant protection officers in enforcing the Article within forty-eight hours of a warning; in certain cases crops may be destroyed WITHOUT INDEMNIFYING THE OWNER, with the agriculture ministry required to introduce a replacement crop. On pesticides it registers and lists authorised products, may analyse a sample to verify a consignment, supervises manufacturers and formulators, and inspects retail shops. Goods imported without a permit are warned for return within a month and otherwise destroyed. Note the site blocks access from IP addresses outside Iran; the IPPC country page carries the named contact. Also under the same organisation: plant quarantine. Standards are a separate body, INSO, renamed from ISIRI in 2011.

complain.n: IFDA — Iran Food and Drug Administration (سازمان غذا و دارو)
complain.d: Handles food labelling; Iran requires GM labelling. THE NUMBER IS 190, the health ministry's national registration and complaints line, and it is the route published by the food and drug deputyships themselves. Complaints are also taken through ONLINE FORMS at the provincial MEDICAL UNIVERSITY food and drug deputyship (moˈāvenat-e ghazā va dāru) — that is the structure worth understanding: IFDA works through the medical universities province by province, so the nearest office is a university deputyship rather than a ministry branch. Those deputyships convene a TECHNICAL-LEGAL COMMISSION ON NON-CONFORMITY (komision-e fanni hoquqi — adam-e entebaq) which rules on products that fail to conform, and separate commissions for cosmetics; they also monitor online sales for criminal content and document digital evidence. IFDA registers and regulates medicines, FOODS, cosmetics, medical devices and supplements. Candid note: published complaints from the public about non-response to the 190 line are easy to find, so expect to have to persist.

complain.d: Inspects imports. The ministry's agricultural quarantine departments sit at the border posts and take instruction by circular. A rule worth knowing: IMPORTERS OF FOOD CROPS MUST SUBMIT AN APPROVED CERTIFICATE FROM AN ACCREDITED DEPARTMENT OF THE EXPORTING COUNTRY stating the maximum permitted pesticide content, and PRODUCTS WITHOUT IT ARE REJECTED AT THE BORDER. On the domestic side, MUSCAT MUNICIPALITY HAS REQUIRED LOCAL FARMS TO LABEL THEIR PRODUCE WITH THE FARM NAME so that anything found wrong can be traced back — farm-level traceability on fresh produce, which is rare. Both measures followed a real case: the UAE banned certain Omani melons, watercress and carrots after finding pesticide residues above maximum limits, and the minister acknowledged publicly that monitoring exports of that volume is difficult and that violations were being pursued. Read with this country's other entry — the separate Consumer Protection Authority.

complain.n: CPA — Consumer Protection Authority (Oman)
complain.d: A CORRECTION: the row named the commerce ministry, but Oman has a SEPARATE statutory Consumer Protection Authority with its own royal-decree Consumer Protection Law, and that is the body that acts. Its published work is enforcement rather than advice: it runs inspection campaigns across all governorates, raids premises and seizes prohibited products, and takes cases to court — the Court of First Instance in Muscat has issued rulings against commercial establishments for breaching the Consumer Protection Law. It asks the public to report suspicious products directly. The Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion holds the neighbouring functions — the Directorate General of Standards and Metrology, the commercial register, and a product-safety portal listing goods certified under the Omani conformity system.

complain.n: Ministry of Public Health — food safety
complain.d: Handles food safety and labelling; Qatar imports nearly all its food. THE NUMBER IS 16000, the unified call centre for the public health sector, and the Food Safety Department publishes what it does with the calls: 181 public complaints responded to in the first half of 2024, against 60,520 imported food shipments inspected at Hamad International Airport, Hamad Port, Al Ruwais Port and the ABU SAMRA LAND BORDER. Its electronic system WATHEQ links imported and exported food with the local market and registers the decisions — in that same half-year, 21,457 food items approved, 883 establishments registered, 625 DESTRUCTION REQUESTS and 102 REQUESTS FOR RE-ANALYSIS. That re-analysis figure matters: a decision on a consignment can be challenged and retested. Central Food Laboratories run under the ministry to ISO/IEC standards. Two other routes exist: the Ministry of Commerce and Industry takes hygiene complaints through the MOCIQatar app under 'shop harmful to health and safety', and the Ministry of Municipality's Health Control Section takes them online and through its 'Oun' app. A National Food Safety Committee decides control issues INCLUDING IMPORT BANS.

complain.n: Public Authority for Food and Nutrition
complain.d: Inspects imports and handles labelling. It acts, publicly and often. PAFN runs INSPECTION DEPARTMENTS BY GOVERNORATE — Capital, Hawalli, Farwaniya, Jahra, Mubarak Al-Kabeer — so there is a local office rather than one national desk, and it publishes the outcome of campaigns: establishments CLOSED, citations issued, and destruction orders for food unfit for consumption. Reported findings include ADULTERATED FOOD PRODUCTS LACKING PROPER IDENTIFICATION LABELS — the mislabelling failure this map tracks — alongside expired licences and unsanitary handling. It works jointly with the Ministry of Interior, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and the Public Authority for Manpower on raids. ITS CENTRAL FOOD TESTING LABORATORY in the Shuwaikh Industrial Area processes around 1,200 SAMPLES A DAY from across Kuwait and from border points, with barcode tracking, testing for bacteria, viruses and other pathogens. PAFN HAS PUBLICLY THANKED MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC WHO REPORTED VIOLATIONS, which is as clear a signal as this file records that reports are acted on. Note Kuwait Municipality also licenses and inspects food establishments.

complain.n: Food Control Section, Public Health Directorate — Ministry of Health (Bahrain)
complain.d: Handles food safety and labelling. The unit is the FOOD CONTROL SECTION inside the PUBLIC HEALTH DIRECTORATE, and its published guidelines set out what an inspector may do: ENTER FACILITIES AND FACTORIES, INSPECT, WITHDRAW SAMPLES, verify certificates and documents, and record violations for JUDICIAL CONTROL — so an inspection can feed a prosecution, not only an administrative penalty. Operating any food activity WITHOUT A LICENCE is itself a violation under the Public Health Law, and the section MAY SUSPEND A LICENCE AT ANY TIME. Bahrain's Director of Public Health has publicly praised the community's role in monitoring and reporting violations and called on residents to cooperate with inspectors — the second Gulf regulator in this file to say so directly. The ministry publishes a HOTLINES page, which is the current number to use. Note the boundary: the Ministry of Industry and Commerce's Consumer Protection Directorate handles price and trading complaints and states that FOOD MATTERS BELONG TO THE HEALTH MINISTRY'S FOOD CONTROL DEPARTMENT; it must answer a complaint within SIXTY DAYS.

complain.n: General Agency for Specialized Inspection (GASI) — DISSOLVED; functions moved to ministries
complain.d: THE BODY THIS ROW NAMED NO LONGER EXISTS. GASI was created by uniting eleven separate inspection agencies and ran roughly 1,600 to 2,200 inspectors across the 21 provinces and Ulaanbaatar. The government decided to dismantle it BY 1 JANUARY 2023, transferring its functions to the line ministries and moving its inspectors with them, with several hundred posts cut. The stated reason was streamlining inspection to create a more business-friendly climate; reporting at the time also noted GASI's reputation for corruption. So a food or agriculture complaint in Mongolia now goes to the relevant line ministry rather than to a single inspection agency, and this map does not yet name which. The National Center for Public Health handles the health side of foodborne illness. Link goes to the national legal information system, since the successor arrangement is defined by the transfer decisions rather than by one agency's page.

test.d: No regional route for detecting engineered material was established for this country. The row previously pointed at laboratories in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, and that grouping does not hold here: the mechanism that shares testing capacity in this direction is membership of the Eurasian Economic Union, whose technical regulations let a laboratory accredited in one member state produce a result recognised in all of them, and this country is not a member. Searches for a designated laboratory for this purpose in the region returned facilities for dangerous human and animal pathogens, which is a different discipline from finding a transgene in seed. So the honest position is that where a sample goes from here has not been established, rather than that it goes east. nearest capable laboratory is in another country and access runs through the regional body.

complain.n: Agency for Plant Protection and Quarantine (Uzbekistan)
complain.d: THE BODY THIS ROW NAMED WAS REPLACED. The Agency for Plant Protection and Quarantine was created on the basis of the State Plant Quarantine Inspection under the Cabinet of Ministers, and is its legal successor for rights, obligations and international treaties. The same decree LIQUIDATED Uzagrokimehimoya and the territorial Agrokimehimoya companies and ABOLISHED the State Commission for Testing and Registration of Chemicals and Plant Protection Products — so the pesticide registration function moved too. Its director is appointed by the President and ITS DECISIONS BIND ministries, departments, local government bodies, economic entities and citizens. Its tasks include agrochemical analysis of soil, quality control of all mineral and microbiological fertilisers supplied to agriculture, and RADIOLOGICAL AND TOXICOLOGICAL ANALYSIS of pesticide residues, nitrates and heavy metal salts in soil and agricultural products — so it is a testing route as well as a complaint one. Bobur Str. 17, Tashkent. The Agency for Plant Quarantine and Protection was ESTABLISHED BY PRESIDENTIAL DECREE IN JULY 2021, so older references to a department of the agriculture ministry predate it. The current instrument is the LAW ON PLANT PROTECTION, ZRU-877 of 9 NOVEMBER 2023 — recent, and it requires legal entities and individuals to meet sanitary standards when STORING, USING, RENDERING HARMLESS AND BURYING chemical protection products and their containers, sets requirements for transport, and provides that where an ECOLOGICALLY HAZARDOUS SITUATION arises from the production, storage, transport or use of highly toxic or radioactive substances used to protect plants, A SPECIAL ZONE IS ESTABLISHED around the facility and along transport routes. That zone-establishing power is worth knowing. IT PUBLISHES AN ANTI-CORRUPTION REPORTING CHANNEL — a Telegram bot, @uzdavkarantin_antikor_bot — which is a distinct route from a technical complaint. 100100 Tashkent, Bobur str., 1st blind alley 17; info@karantin.uz.

complain.n: Sanitary and Epidemiological Service
complain.d: Handles food safety and labelling. The Service of Sanitary and Epidemiological Welfare and Public Health was ESTABLISHED IN 2019, succeeding the Soviet-era SES founded in 1952, and it operates through TERRITORIAL DEPARTMENTS across the country rather than from Tashkent alone — so there is a regional office to approach. It is named in the 2023 plant protection law alongside the quarantine agency, so the two share the ground where chemical plant protection meets human health.

complain.n: Biosecurity Division / Samoa Quarantine Service — Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries
complain.d: The office this country has designated as its official contact point under Article VIII.2 of the International Plant Protection Convention, as published by the IPPC Secretariat. Arriving seed, plant material and cargo are inspected here, which is where an organism never approved for release would turn up. No website is published in that source, so this names the office without linking it. It is a plant health body: it does not authorise a release, and it is not the biosafety regulator. The IPPC country page is the link here; the IPPC contacts entry in this box explains what that record gives and where it lags. The instrument is the QUARANTINE (BIOSECURITY) ACT 2005, and it is drafted broadly: biosecurity covers examination, exclusion, detention, observation, SEGREGATION, ISOLATION, protection, TESTING, treatment and regulation of conveyances, installations, PEOPLE and regulated articles, aimed at preventing or controlling the introduction, establishment or spread of anything that could significantly damage human beings, animals, plants, THE ENVIRONMENT OR ECONOMIC ACTIVITIES — environmental harm is inside the test, not adjacent to it. Two powers stand out. A quarantine officer may REQUIRE THE COMMISSIONER OF POLICE and any ministry or statutory corporation, including the airports and ports authorities, TO USE THEIR POWERS AND RESOURCES to assist in controlling or eradicating a pest or disease. And on scientific advice the Minister may DECLARE AN AREA OF LAND, WATER OR SEA FREE of specific pests or diseases and impose controls on the movement of humans, animals, plants and goods to maintain it. The Act also defines BENEFICIAL ORGANISMS — self-replicating biotic entities used for pest control. All plant products, fresh or dried, living or dead, must be declared and carry an import permit. The service runs incineration of non-compliant or seized commodities and post-entry quarantine.

complain.n: Department of Biosecurity Vanuatu, Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries, Forestry and Biosecurity
complain.d: The office this country has designated as its official contact point under Article VIII.2 of the International Plant Protection Convention, as published by the IPPC Secretariat. Arriving seed, plant material and cargo are inspected here, which is where an organism never approved for release would turn up. No website is published in that source, so this names the office without linking it. It is a plant health body: it does not authorise a release, and it is not the biosafety regulator. The IPPC country page is the link here; the IPPC contacts entry in this box explains what that record gives and where it lags. The department was created in FEBRUARY 2013 by splitting the former Department of Livestock and Quarantine Services into Biosecurity Vanuatu and a separate Livestock department, so older citations to DLQS predate it. Its legal framework is the PLANT PROTECTION ACT [CAP 239], the Animal Importation and Quarantine Act [CAP 201], the Animal Disease (Control) Act [CAP 220], the Meat Industry Act and the KAVA ACT No. 7 of 2002. THE SEED RULE IS THE THING TO KNOW: seeds require an import permit AND MUST BE SOURCED FROM AN APPROVED SEED COMPANY ON A LIST MAINTAINED BY THE DEPARTMENT — seeds not from an approved company ARE DETAINED FOR DESTRUCTION, and seeds arriving by post are inspected at the Post Office by a Biosecurity Officer. An approved-supplier list for seed is rare and directly usable. Permits must be applied for BEFORE shipment by sea, or 24 hours before airfreight. Its mandate includes surveillance on ALL MAJOR PRODUCING ISLANDS and containing or eradicating regulated pests already present. Offices at Tagabe Road, Port Vila, and Biosecurity North at Luganville; permits run through the Vanuatu Electronic Single Window.

complain.n: Biosecurity Solomon Islands (BSI) — Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock
complain.d: The office this country has designated as its official contact point under Article VIII.2 of the International Plant Protection Convention, as published by the IPPC Secretariat. Arriving seed, plant material and cargo are inspected here, which is where an organism never approved for release would turn up. No website is published in that source, so this names the office without linking it. It is a plant health body: it does not authorise a release, and it is not the biosafety regulator. The IPPC country page is the link here; the IPPC contacts entry in this box explains what that record gives and where it lags. The instrument is the BIOSECURITY ACT 2013 (No. 3 of 2013) with Biosecurity Regulations 2015. BSI states it works INSIDE, BEYOND AND AT the borders, so post-entry problems are within its remit. The seed position is unusually well documented: BSI has publicly warned that IMPORTING SEEDS FOR PLANTING OF ANY SORT, AND SELLING THEM, IS ILLEGAL WITHOUT AN IMPORT PERMIT, and in January 2021 it ran a JOINT OPERATION WITH THE ROYAL SOLOMON ISLANDS POLICE FORCE against eight Honiara shops selling planting seed without one — items confiscated and destroyed. Its stated objections are worth repeating because they apply to seed sold anywhere: packets labelled in languages buyers cannot read, no botanical names, no numbering or coding to link packets to a list, AND LABELLING DIFFERENT FROM THE CONTENTS. Section 9 restricts import of regulated articles; section 47 lets officers inspect, detain and confiscate; section 3 applies to all persons and goods regardless of origin — BSI has stated expressly that another country's clearance does not override Solomon Islands law. A specific permit covers a single consignment and may carry an expiry date.

complain.d: The office this country has designated as its official contact point under Article VIII.2 of the International Plant Protection Convention, as published by the IPPC Secretariat. The division has ITS OWN SITE, quarantine.gov.to, rather than only a ministry page. Its stated objective is protecting Tonga's ECONOMY, ENVIRONMENT AND PEOPLE'S HEALTH from pests and diseases — both preventing arrival of exotic pests AND controlling those already present, so post-entry problems are in scope. Its structure names the functions worth knowing: legislation, trade facilitation, IMPORT RISK ANALYSIS, market access, export, import, airport services, vessel clearance, and OUTER ISLANDS OPERATIONS — that last one matters across 169 islands, where a single Nuku'alofa office would leave most of the country unreached. Import risk analysis being a named standing function means an assessment is a normal instrument here, not an exception. Food safety on the market sits with the health ministry rather than a separate food authority, and Customs under the revenue ministry controls import and export. P.O. Box 14, Nuku'alofa.

complain.d: The office this country has designated as its official contact point under Article VIII.2 of the International Plant Protection Convention, as published by the IPPC Secretariat. Arriving seed, plant material and cargo are inspected here, which is where an organism never approved for release would turn up. No website is published in that source, so this names the office without linking it. It is a plant health body: it does not authorise a release, and it is not the biosafety regulator. The IPPC country page is the link here; the IPPC contacts entry in this box explains what that record gives and where it lags. A CORRECTION on where this now sits: BIOSECURITY IS RUN FROM THE BUREAU OF CUSTOMS AND BORDER PROTECTION, not from the natural resources ministry, and the agriculture portfolio has moved into a Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and the Environment (MAFE). Biosecurity enforces import and export rules on animal and plant material at all points of entry, monitors movements against APPROVED LISTS OF ALLOWED PLANTS AND ANIMALS, disposes of confiscated product, and — the part that matters here — carries out POST-BORDER work on invasive species eradication and control. Everyone arriving must DECLARE all risk goods: plants, plant products, animals, animal products, any food, wooden articles, SOIL and used materials. Under the Plant and Animal Quarantine Regulations plants for consignment to Palau must be grown in a place approved by the Chief of Agriculture, screened for pests and certified. Palau also runs an INTER-ISLAND BIOSECURITY framework, controlling movement BETWEEN its own states and islands — rare, and directly relevant where a release on one island could spread. biosecurity@bcbp.pw.

complain.n: Plant Protection Department — Ministry of Agriculture (Barbados)
complain.d: The office this country has designated as its official contact point under Article VIII.2 of the International Plant Protection Convention, as published by the IPPC Secretariat. Arriving seed, plant material and cargo are inspected here, which is where an organism never approved for release would turn up. No website is published in that source, so this names the office without linking it. It is a plant health body: it does not authorise a release, and it is not the biosafety regulator. The IPPC country page is the link here; the IPPC contacts entry in this box explains what that record gives and where it lags. The Plant Pathology Unit is one of FOUR units in the Plant Protection Department, and naming the department is more useful than naming the unit: pathology, ENTOMOLOGY, the PESTICIDE CONTROL BOARD and PLANT QUARANTINE work as an integrated group. That matters for routing — pathology diagnoses, quarantine imposes conditions or restrictions on incoming plants and live agricultural products on pathology's advice, and the Pesticide Control Board handles chemicals. The department prepares the COUNTRY PEST LIST, conducts PEST RISK ANALYSES and surveillance under the WTO SPS Agreement, and runs PLANT CLINICS open to farmers, hobbyists and the general public — which is a diagnostic route an ordinary grower can use. Its scope covers all plant life whether grown locally, entering or leaving Barbados. Graeme Hall, Christ Church. Note the IPPC contact for this unit was registered in 2009.

complain.n: BNSI — Barbados National Standards Institution
complain.d: A CORRECTION on who enforces. BNSI is not a government agency: it was established in 1973 under the COMPANIES ACT as a joint venture between the Government of Barbados and the private sector, a non-profit benevolent organisation incorporated by private law and recognised by government, given legal force through the Standards Act 2006 and the Weights and Measures Act. It prepares standards, tests, certifies, accredits and calibrates — with the Government Analytical Services it tests conformity to 43 mandatory standards covering food products, soils, materials and textiles. But ENFORCEMENT of food standards is carried out by Standards Inspectors from the DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE AND CONSUMER AFFAIRS, supported by BNSI's interpretations. BNSI is also the Codex contact point and the WTO/TBT enquiry point. Note the site moved to bnsibarbados.org.

complain.d: The office this country has designated as its official contact point under Article VIII.2 of the International Plant Protection Convention, as published by the IPPC Secretariat. Arriving seed, plant material and cargo are inspected here, which is where an organism never approved for release would turn up. No website is published in that source, so this names the office without linking it. It is a plant health body: it does not authorise a release, and it is not the biosafety regulator. The IPPC country page is the link here; the IPPC contacts entry in this box explains what that record gives and where it lags. The single SPS authority for the Bahamas — animal health, plant health AND food — created to bring those functions into one coordinated body, and it regulates all imported animal, plant and food products. Two practical points. All animal, plant and FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS must register with BAHFSA to obtain a business licence, and the registration carries an ANNUAL INSPECTION. And its Authorised Officers hold wide statutory powers under the Food Safety and Quality Act: on showing a badge they may enter any place where food is produced, prepared, stored, sold, transported, imported or exported, TAKE SAMPLES FOR TESTING, stop and search a vehicle believed to be carrying food, open and examine any package, TAKE PHOTOGRAPHS AND VIDEO of the business including of records requested, and read measuring instruments on site. It is the Codex contact point and the WOAH delegate. Note two live domains, bahfsabahamas.com and the bahamas.gov.bs agency page.

complain.n: Crop Protection & Quarantine Unit — Ministry of Agriculture (Saint Lucia)
complain.d: The office this country has designated as its official contact point under Article VIII.2 of the International Plant Protection Convention, as published by the IPPC Secretariat. Arriving seed, plant material and cargo are inspected here, which is where an organism never approved for release would turn up. No website is published in that source, so this names the office without linking it. It is a plant health body: it does not authorise a release, and it is not the biosafety regulator. The IPPC country page is the link here; the IPPC contacts entry in this box explains what that record gives and where it lags. The instruments are the PLANT PROTECTION ACT No. 21 of 1988 with the Plant Protection Regulations S.I. 66 of 1995, and the PESTICIDES AND TOXIC CHEMICAL CONTROL ACT Cap. 11.15, under which a Pesticides and Toxic Chemicals Control Board runs licensing, enforcement and advice to the Minister. Three things a reader can use. A PLANT IMPORT PERMIT is required, and the Quarantine Unit REVIEWS EVERY APPLICATION BY PERFORMING A PEST RISK ANALYSIS to check the pest status of the country of origin at the time of application — two weeks or less for previously approved material, longer for a new commodity or a new origin. SOIL ENTRY IS STRICTLY PROHIBITED except for laboratory testing or recognised scientific research. And the ministry PUBLISHES ITS LIST OF REGISTERED PESTICIDES with product name, active ingredient, registration number, pesticide type and formulation code. The Board has publicly warned of a rise in unregistered pesticides being ordered and imported, noting some may be restricted or banned in their country of origin. Offices in Castries and Vieux Fort. Note the ministry's name has changed.

complain.n: Pest Management Unit; Ministry of Agriculture
complain.d: The office this country has designated as its official contact point under Article VIII.2 of the International Plant Protection Convention, as published by the IPPC Secretariat. Arriving seed, plant material and cargo are inspected here, which is where an organism never approved for release would turn up. No website is published in that source, so this names the office without linking it. It is a plant health body: it does not authorise a release, and it is not the biosafety regulator. The IPPC country page is the link here; the IPPC contacts entry in this box explains what that record gives and where it lags. Two instruments and two bodies. The PLANT PROTECTION ACT No. 19 of 1986 lets the Minister PROHIBIT OR RESTRICT the entry of any planting material, fruit, vegetable, plant product, plant pest, SOIL or other non-plant article that may result in the entry or movement of plant pests, and it carries a duty on an OCCUPIER TO NOTIFY PESTS, power for officers to serve notice on an occupier requiring action, exclusion of government liability with a power to compensate, and a Plant Protection Board on whose advice the Minister acts. Separately the PESTICIDES CONTROL ACT, approved 1973 and amended 1979, controls importation, sale, storage and use of pesticides through a PESTICIDES CONTROL BOARD chaired from the agriculture ministry, with a quorum of five and inspectors assigned by the Minister; Cabinet reappointed the Board in February 2025, so it is functioning. Import of plants or plant material requires a phytosanitary certificate, and cruise and cargo vessels releasing anything agricultural are regulated too. Botanic Gardens, Tanteen, St George's. The Grenada Bureau of Standards is the Codex contact.

Arriving seed, plant material and cargo are inspected here, which is where an organism never approved for release would turn up. No website is published in that source, so this names the office without linking it. It is a plant health body: it does not authorise a release, and it is not the biosafety regulator. The IPPC country page is the link here; the IPPC contacts entry in this box explains what that record gives and where it lags. It is the designated national plant protection organisation, and its mandate comes from the PLANT PROTECTION ACT No. 18 OF 2012 — which replaced Cap. 329 of 1941, so older citations to that Act or to S.R.O. No. 10 of 1959 predate it. The Act creates a PLANT PROTECTION BOARD that determines the need for regulations, advises the Minister, advises on WHEN A PHYTOSANITARY EMERGENCY IS DECLARED, and presides over the PHYTOSANITARY EMERGENCY FUND — a standing fund for exactly the situation this map documents. The Board was first appointed by Cabinet in June 2015. The division also chairs the Coordinating Council on Agricultural Health and Food Safety, formed by Cabinet decision in February 2015, which is the forum where public and private stakeholders meet on these questions. Practically: an import permit is required for cuttings, seeds, tubers for planting, IN VITRO AND MICROPROPAGATIVE PLANT MATERIAL and live plants, and every inbound regulated consignment needs a phytosanitary certificate from the exporting country's plant protection organisation. It has its own site, plantprotection.gov.ag, and a Barbuda sub-unit.

complain.d: The office this country has designated as its official contact point under Article VIII.2 of the International Plant Protection Convention, as published by the IPPC Secretariat. The unit to name is PLANT PROTECTION AND QUARANTINE, the lead institution for protecting agricultural resources from plant and animal pests and diseases, with its legislative authority in the PLANT PROTECTION AND QUARANTINE ACT 1986; monitoring of SPS measures sits with it too. Beside it, the PESTICIDE CONTROL BOARD at the Botanical Gardens holds the chemicals: anyone importing a registered pesticide must first obtain a LICENCE, granted for ONE SHIPMENT and valid THREE MONTHS, presented with customs documents — and A LIST OF REGISTERED PESTICIDES IS AVAILABLE AT THE BOARD'S OFFICE, which a reader should check before assuming a product is lawful here. Also in the division: a PRODUCE CHEMIST UNIT and a plant propagation unit running citrus certification. The Dominica Bureau of Standards, at the National Centre of Testing Excellence, is the Codex contact point and the testing address. Botanical Gardens, Roseau.

complain.n: Plant Protection and Quarantine Unit — Ministry of Agriculture (Saint Vincent and the Grenadines)
complain.d: The office this country has designated as its official contact point under Article VIII.2 of the International Plant Protection Convention, as published by the IPPC Secretariat. Arriving seed, plant material and cargo are inspected here, which is where an organism never approved for release would turn up. No website is published in that source, so this names the office without linking it. It is a plant health body: it does not authorise a release, and it is not the biosafety regulator. The IPPC country page is the link here; the IPPC contacts entry in this box explains what that record gives and where it lags. The instrument is the PLANT PROTECTION ACT No. 15 of 2005. Import requires permission from the unit in advance, and an import permit sets out the permitted commodities and conditions; A PEST RISK ASSESSMENT MAY BE REQUIRED FIRST, WHICH CAN TAKE UP TO TWO MONTHS — so an objection has a real window. Entry is only through PRESCRIBED PORTS, and on the NPPO's advice the Minister may require that certain plants, plant products or regulated articles NOT BE IMPORTED AT ALL. A consignment is released only if an inspector determines it presents no risk of introducing or spreading pests, and an inspector may CONFISCATE AND DISPOSE of regulated articles left unclaimed after entry or treatment. The customs officer must have a plant protection officer examine any package containing or suspected of containing plants, SOIL or living insects. Also relevant here: the PLANT BREEDERS' PROTECTION BILL 2019 created variety rights, with exemptions for private non-commercial acts, experimental acts and breeding other varieties, and provision for COMPULSORY LICENCES. Richmond Hill, Kingstown.

complain.n: BAHA — Belize Agricultural Health Authority, Plant Health Department
complain.d: The office this country has designated as its official contact point under Article VIII.2 of the International Plant Protection Convention, as published by the IPPC Secretariat. Arriving seed, plant material and cargo are inspected here, which is where an organism never approved for release would turn up. No website is published in that source, so this names the office without linking it. It is a plant health body: it does not authorise a release, and it is not the biosafety regulator. The IPPC country page is the link here; the IPPC contacts entry in this box explains what that record gives and where it lags. A statutory body established in 2000 under the BAHA Act (Chapter 47 of 1999, now Chapter 211), which took over the plant protection and animal health services of the agriculture ministry. Four technical departments — Plant Health, Animal Health, Food Safety and Quarantine — so this is a single competent authority for agricultural health and food safety. THE POINT THAT MATTERS MOST HERE IS IN THE ACT'S OWN DEFINITIONS: 'planting material' includes trees, shrubs, vines, cuttings, grafts, scions, buds, bulbs, roots, seeds OR ANY OTHER PLANT, BE IT GENETICALLY ENGINEERED, ALTERED OR OTHERWISE, capable of being propagated or cultured from tissue. Engineered material is inside the definition by name, which is rare in a plant health statute. The Act also carries Prevention Orders, PEST CONTROL NOTICES, occupier responsibility, power of entry and imposition of quarantine, post-entry quarantine and COMPENSATION provisions. Note inspection fees are payable by the importer, and BAHA runs national accreditation programmes for veterinarians and for LABORATORIES. Central Farm, Cayo District.

complain.n: GNBS — Guyana National Bureau of Standards
complain.d: Handles food labelling standards. Established March 1985 under the Standards Act No. 11 of 1984, a statutory corporation governed by a National Standards Council. Its own stated objectives include safeguarding consumers by ENFORCING standards against subpar products and services, and its services include product inspection, testing, certification and verification. Two roles make it the enquiry point as well: it is Guyana's WTO/TBT National Enquiry Point and the FAO/WHO CODEX ALIMENTARIUS CONTACT POINT — so it is also the body that knows which other national authority handles a given food question. Note it is a self-revenue-generating agency as well as government funded, and the parent ministry has changed name repeatedly. LINK CHECKED AND FOUND DEAD: the page or host no longer answers. decides.n: Ministry of Agriculture, Natural Resources and Rural Development
decides.d: In 2010, after the earthquake, Monsanto offered several hundred tonnes of hybrid seed as a donation and Haitian peasant organisations publicly burned it, arguing it would displace local varieties and create dependency on purchased seed. It remains the most direct rejection of donated seed anywhere, and it was made by farmers rather than by a government. The Clearing-House entry in this box explains what a country profile holds and what a thin one means.

complain.n: Direction Quarantaine (DQCSPAP) — MARNDR (Haïti)
complain.d: Plant protection; inspects imports and seed. THE OPERATING BODY HAS ITS OWN SITE: the Direction de la Quarantaine et du Contrôle Sanitaire des Produits Agricoles et de la Pêche (DQCSPAP), agriculturequarantaine.gouv.ht, which covers BOTH plant and animal sides. It runs a Système d'Information de la Direction Quarantaine (SIQ) built with IICA, and publishes the procedure for requesting a phytosanitary or zoosanitary certificate. Also inside MARNDR: the UNITÉ DE PROTECTION SANITAIRE (UPS) at Damien, Route Nationale #1, which is Haiti's WOAH delegate address, and a VETERINARY AND FOOD QUALITY CONTROL LABORATORY that has moved into food standards work and is intended to become an autonomous institute. The BUREAU HAÏTIEN DE NORMALISATION is the Codex contact point. Note the division with health: MSPP regulates hygiene and food safety AT THE POINT OF SALE for products of animal and plant origin and develops inspection norms WITH MARNDR, and identifies cases of food poisoning — so production and border sit with agriculture, retail with health.

complain.n: Ministère de la Santé — contrôle alimentaire
complain.d: Handles food safety. MSPP sets health standards and inspects to reduce foodborne illness, and its remit is specifically THE POINT OF SALE — hygiene and food safety for products of animal and plant origin destined for human consumption — with inspection norms developed JOINTLY WITH MARNDR. It also identifies cases of FOOD POISONING AND ZOONOSES. Under the 2017 food fortification law it runs the RANFOSE programme, working directly with WHEAT FLOUR MILLS, iodised salt producers and importers of flour, edible oil and salt — so it has standing relationships with the millers and importers, which is where a question about what is in the national flour supply would start.

legal.d: The peasant movement that publicly burned the donated hybrid seed in 2010 — the most direct rejection of donated seed anywhere, made by farmers rather than a government. Known in Kreyòl as Mouvman Peyizan Papay. Founded 20 March 1973 at Papaye in the Central Plateau, recognised as being of public utility in the official gazette Le Moniteur on 5 September 1990, and organised into roughly 4,500 groupings totalling some 60,000 members. It runs savings and credit cooperatives against a rural lending system charging interest reported up to 480% a year, under which farmers sell land to repay. Agronomy faculties send students there for agroecology placements. A reader looking for who represents smallholders in Haiti is looking at a body with a legal status, a gazette citation and a membership roll, not a campaign.

complain.n: AGASA — Agence Gabonaise de Sécurité Alimentaire
complain.d: Inspects imports and seed. Created by decree in 2011 (n°0292/PR/MAEPDR of 18 February 2011, amended 2013), AGASA is BOTH the food safety agency AND GABON'S NATIONAL PLANT PROTECTION ORGANISATION (ONPV) — so food and plant health are one address here. Its stated purpose is protecting consumers by acting against the marketing of food unfit for consumption. IT PUBLISHES A PESTICIDES SECTION with the working definition it applies, which is broad: any substance, combination of substances, OR MICRO-ORGANISM INCLUDING VIRUSES intended to repel, destroy or combat pests during production, processing, storage, transport or marketing of food, agricultural products, wood or animal feed — covering both agricultural phytopharmaceuticals and industrial and domestic biocides. A definition that names viruses and micro-organisms reaches engineered biocontrol agents. REGISTRATION IS REGIONAL: Gabon sits under the COMITÉ INTER-ÉTATS D'HOMOLOGATION DES PESTICIDES DE L'AFRIQUE CENTRALE (CPAC) for the CEMAC states, so what may be sold in Gabon is decided in a regional committee — the Central African counterpart to the Sahelian committee named elsewhere in this file. Immeuble Bel Espace 2, Libreville; info@agasa.site.

test.d: The sub-regional laboratory for analysis of pesticides and pesticide residues in food in Central Africa, run under CEMAC. Its Biology Department carries an OGM/mycotoxins sector alongside veterinary, bacteriology, virology and biopesticides work, so detection capacity for engineered material exists here as one department of an institution built primarily for residue analysis rather than as a dedicated GMO laboratory. Accreditation across the sub-region is the weak point: the CEMAC and CEEAC laboratory mapping carried out under the EU-funded PACIE programme covered 47 testing laboratories in seven countries and found good technical competence but a general need for support to reach ISO/IEC 17025, so a result may not carry formal recognition. Samples otherwise go to Cameroon's national laboratories rather than to West Africa. nearest capable laboratory is in another country and access runs through the regional body.

complain.n: SQAV — Service de la Quarantaine Animale et Végétale (RDC)
complain.d: Inspects imports. THE CORRECT NAME IS SQAV — Service de la Quarantaine ANIMALE ET VÉGÉTALE — covering animal and plant together, a specialised service of the agriculture ministry attached to the SECRÉTARIAT GÉNÉRAL À L'AGRICULTURE, PÊCHE ET ÉLEVAGE, headquartered in Kinshasa. Its founding text gives it zoo- and phytosanitary surveillance and quarantine management across the national territory, AND EXPRESSLY THE POLICE FUNCTION for that; it may call on the specialised services of other ministries. It is led by a Coordonnateur National appointed by the Minister, WITH PROVINCIAL REPRESENTATION. Two candid points a reader should weigh. Its coordinator has PUBLICLY APPEALED FOR SUPPORT to allow the service to cover ALL the country's borders — an admission that it currently does not. And its mandate includes GENERATING NON-TAX REVENUE FOR THE TREASURY, so its inspections carry a fee-collection purpose alongside the protective one. Seed multiplication sits with INERA, under the scientific research ministry, which produces foundation and base seed. A new SERVICE NATIONAL DE SÉCURISATION ET DE PROTECTION AGROÉCOLOGIQUE (SNSPA) was created by ministerial order on 26 February 2026.

complain.n: Serviços de Sanidade Vegetal — MINAGRIF, under Lei n.º 5/21 (Angola)
complain.d: Inspects imports and seed. The current instrument is the LEI DA SANIDADE VEGETAL, LEI N.º 5/21 of 3 February 2021 — recent, and it applies to natural and legal persons, PUBLIC AND PRIVATE, engaged in agricultural or forestry exploitation, SCIENTIFIC STUDIES, handling, production, transport, marketing, import and export of plants, and storage and packaging — so a research release is inside its scope. THE SEED PROVISION IS THE ONE TO KNOW: a prior import licence for SEEDS AND PLANTS FOR PLANTING depends on presenting a licence authorising their import ISSUED BY THE AUTORIDADE NACIONAL DE SEMENTES, so seed imports need TWO authorisations, phytosanitary and seed-authority. A phytosanitary certificate is compulsory on entry of any plant or plant product. The Entidade Fitossanitária publishes the lists of CONDITIONED OR PROHIBITED import species and of QUARANTINE PESTS, and ESTABLISHES THE QUARANTINE REGIME — including declaring a state of phytosanitary alert or emergency, when the responsibilities of related authorities must be defined. Angola has stated an intention to CREATE AN INSTITUTO DE PROTECÇÃO DE PLANTAS. Food quality control sits with SNCQA, created by Decreto Presidencial 138/19; seed with SENSE.
